7.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
7.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

8.meaning: It was cut up, severed, and torn apart into pieces; thoroughly broken open or rent asunder. A passive sense with an intensive force of repeated, complete cutting.
8.grammar: A past-tense passive verb in an intensive form, third-person feminine singular. The inner vowels (u–i) mark it passive — 'it was cut' rather than 'it cut.' The intensive form conveys thorough, repeated cutting ('cut to pieces'), and the suffix -t signals a feminine subject.

9.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
9.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

10.meaning: Garments — clothes, articles of dress; the plural of thawb (a garment or robe).
10.grammar: A broken (internal) plural noun. The -un ending is nominative (subject case) with tanwīn, the final -n marking indefiniteness: 'garments' in general rather than particular known ones.
10.root: ث-و-ب (th-w-b) — garment; also to return (a garment 'returns' to cover the body)

11.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
11.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

12.meaning: A noun meaning 'fire' — blazing, burning flame; also evoking, by extension, the Fire of punishment.
12.grammar: An indefinite noun. The ending -in is the genitive case with nunation (the -n sound marking 'a/an'): the genitive typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun in an 'of/from' relationship.
12.root: ن-و-ر (n-w-r) — to burn, blaze; fire, heat

13.meaning: Is poured / will be poured — liquid being poured out, with the doer left unnamed (passive).
13.grammar: A passive present-tense verb: the internal vowels (yu-…-a-) signal the passive, so the subject is the thing poured, not the pourer. The final -u is the indicative ending — the default 'plain statement' mood of the present tense, describing what happens or will happen.

14.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
14.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

15.meaning: Above / on top of / over — the position higher than or upon something.
15.grammar: A noun of place meaning 'above', used adverbially. Its -i ending is genitive, the case that typically links it to a following noun ('above … OF something') or follows a preposition. So: 'above / on top of'.
15.root: ف-و-ق (f-w-q) — to be above, surpass; height, superiority

16.meaning: Their heads — the heads of a group of people.
16.grammar: A plural noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The -i ending is genitive: it typically follows a preposition or links the noun to another word ('of…'). The suffix -him means 'their' (of them, masculine plural); its final -u in the transliteration is just a helping vowel used when the next word begins with a connecting alif.

17.meaning: The scalding water — ḥamīm is water heated to the extreme of boiling; the word carries the sense of intense, searing heat.
17.grammar: A definite noun. The -u ending is nominative: the case of the subject or the thing being talked about in a sentence. The l- prefix is the definite article 'the' (the initial a- of al- merges into the preceding word in recitation).
17.root: ح-م-م (ḥ-m-m) — intense heat, to heat water

1.meaning: Is melted / will be melted — caused to dissolve away by heat, with the doer left unnamed (passive).
1.grammar: A passive present-tense verb: the yu-…-a- vowel pattern marks the passive, so the subject is what gets melted. The final -u is the indicative ending, the plain statement mood of the present tense.
1.root: ص-ه-ر (ṣ-h-r) — to melt, fuse by heat

2.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
2.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

3.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
3.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

4.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
4.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

5.meaning: A noun with possessor, meaning 'their bellies / their stomachs / insides'. It denotes the abdomen or inner cavity, the part of the body that holds what is eaten.
5.grammar: A plural noun (singular baṭn 'belly') with the attached pronoun -him 'their' (masculine plural). The -i vowel before the pronoun reflects the genitive case, which is also the case a noun takes when something is possessed by an attached pronoun ('the bellies OF them').
5.root: ب-ط-ن (b-ṭ-n) — belly, inner part, that which is hidden inside

6.meaning: And the skins — the outer skin or hide; plural of jild.
6.grammar: A definite plural noun joined by wa- 'and'. The -u ending is nominative: it marks the word as a subject or as an item coordinated with another subject-case word.

1.meaning: A connector meaning 'and', joined to a phrase 'for them' or 'they have' — literally 'and to/for them', expressing that something belongs to or is owed to a group.
1.grammar: Two prefixes on a pronoun: wa- means 'and', and the preposition la- means 'for/to'. The pronoun -hum means 'them', a group of males or a mixed group. The preposition la- attached to a pronoun commonly conveys possession or entitlement — 'they have' or 'for them (belongs) …'.

2.meaning: Maces / hooked rods — heavy iron instruments for striking and subduing; plural of miqmaʿa, an instrument of restraint.

parts.en: maces, rods of subduing (plural of miqmaʿa)

2.grammar: A broken plural on the pattern maCāCiC, which names instruments — 'things one subdues with'. The -u ending is nominative (subject case). Note it takes no tanwīn (-n): this plural pattern belongs to a class of nouns (diptotes) that never take the indefinite -n even when indefinite.
2.root: ق-م-ع (q-m-ʿ) — to subdue, restrain, beat down

3.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
3.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

4.meaning: Iron — the metal, emblematic of hardness and strength.
4.grammar: A noun in the genitive: the -in ending combines the genitive case vowel -i, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… of iron') or follows a preposition, with tanwīn, the -n of indefiniteness ('iron' as a material, not a specific piece).

1.meaning: 'whenever / every time' — a compound expressing that something recurs each and every time a condition is met.
1.grammar: A compound of kull ('every', in the accusative -a used adverbially) and mā ('what / the time that'). Together it works as a conditional time-word, 'each time that …', linking a repeated condition to its repeated result.

2.meaning: A verb (past, masculine plural) meaning 'they wanted, willed, intended, desired' something.
2.grammar: Past tense, fourth-form verb. The suffix -ū marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they') in the completed (perfect) aspect — an action or intention presented as accomplished. (The silent alif after the wāw is a spelling convention.)
2.root: ر-و-د (r-w-d) — to seek, want, will; to go to and fro

3.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
3.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

4.meaning: They go out / depart / exit: to leave a place, to come or go forth from within.
4.grammar: A present/subjunctive verb of Form I, third-person masculine plural ('they go out'). The ya- prefix marks a third-person subject and the -ū ending marks a plural of males. The normally-final -na is dropped, signalling the subjunctive or jussive mood that follows certain particles.
4.root: خ-ر-ج (kh-r-j) — to go out, to exit, to emerge

5.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'min' ('from / out of / some of') joined to the pronoun 'it' (feminine). Together: 'from it / out of it / of it,' indicating a source or a portion taken from a feminine thing.
5.grammar: A preposition 'min' with the attached pronoun '-hā' ('it/her'), referring to a feminine noun. 'Min' indicates origin, source, or a part taken from a whole; the attached pronoun is in the object form required after a preposition.

6.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
6.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

7.meaning: Anguish — a grief or distress so heavy it covers and smothers the heart, from a root meaning 'to envelop'.
7.grammar: A noun in the genitive: the -in ending is the genitive case vowel plus tanwīn (indefinite -n). The genitive typically follows a preposition or ties the word to a preceding noun ('… of anguish').
7.root: غ-م-م (gh-m-m) — to cover, veil; grief that envelops

8.meaning: A verb meaning 'they were returned' or 'they were sent back' — the passive of bringing someone back to a former place or state, with the doer unnamed.
8.grammar: A past-tense passive verb. The 'u-' opening vowel marks it as passive ('they were returned'), leaving the one who returns them unstated. The '-ū' ending marks the affected party as 'they' (masculine plural). This is a Form IV verb: to bring/send back.
8.root: ع-و-د (ʿ-w-d) — to return, come back; (Form IV) to send back

9.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
9.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

10.meaning: 'And taste!' — a command to taste; beyond the literal act of tasting with the tongue, it commonly means to undergo and experience something firsthand (such as a punishment or consequence).
10.grammar: Opens with wa- ('and'). The verb is a command (imperative) addressed to a masculine plural group: 'you all, taste!'. The long -ū ending is the plural marker on a command directed at more than one person.

11.meaning: Torment, punishment, or chastisement — severe, painful suffering imposed as a penalty.
11.grammar: A singular noun. The final -a (fatḥa) marks the accusative case, the form used for a direct object of a verb, or for the first noun of a possessive pair ('the punishment of …') when that whole phrase is itself an object.

12.meaning: The burning — intense, consuming fire; a blaze that scorches and burns up. An intensive term for fierce flame.
12.grammar: The noun 'the burning' with the definite article al- ('the'). The final -i ending is genitive, the case used after a preposition or to link to a preceding noun ('… of …'). The faʿīl pattern here gives an intensive sense of a fierce, consuming fire.
12.root: ح-ر-ق (ḥ-r-q) — to burn, scorch, set ablaze

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
2.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

3.meaning: "He admits / causes to enter" — the causative of 'enter': not to go in oneself but to bring someone in, to grant entry, characteristically used of Allah admitting people into the Garden.
3.grammar: The yu- prefix means 'he' in the present/future tense; its u-vowel (yu- rather than ya-) is the signature of the causative pattern (Form IV): 'make someone enter' instead of 'enter'. The final -u is the plain indicative mood — a straightforward statement of what he does or will do.

4.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
4.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

5.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
5.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

6.meaning: A two-part word: 'and' + 'they did / worked / performed.' The verb denotes doing deeds, working, putting effort into action — practical doing as opposed to mere speaking or believing.
6.grammar: A conjunction 'wa' + a past-tense verb, 3rd person masculine plural. The -ū ending marks the subject as 'they' (a group of males or a mixed group): 'and they did / worked.'

7.meaning: 'The righteous deeds / good works' — the definite plural of a word meaning that which is sound, wholesome, upright, and beneficial. As a noun it refers to good, virtuous actions that set things right.
7.grammar: A definite sound feminine plural noun ('the good deeds'). The -i ending is the oblique case used by feminine plurals to mark either the genitive ('… of …' / after a preposition) or the accusative (direct object); for this plural pattern the accusative and genitive share the same -i ending.
7.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — to be sound, good, upright, set right

8.meaning: 'Gardens' — the plural of a lush, walled garden thick with trees whose foliage covers the ground. The root sense is concealment by dense greenery; it is the standard word for the gardens of Paradise.
8.grammar: An indefinite sound feminine plural noun ('gardens'). The '-in' (tanwīn) ending marks it as indefinite ('some gardens'), and for this plural form it stands in the oblique case (genitive or accusative), used after prepositions/possessives or as a direct object.
8.root: ج-ن-ن (j-n-n) — to cover, conceal, hide (hence a dense garden)

9.meaning: A verb 'it flows, runs, streams' — used of water and rivers moving along, and of things that run or course freely. It describes continuous, ongoing motion.
9.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, 3rd person feminine singular. The ta- prefix here marks a feminine 'it/she' subject. The verb describes an ongoing or habitual action: 'it flows / keeps flowing.'

10.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
10.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

11.meaning: 'Beneath it / underneath it' — the noun for the underside or lower region of something, with an attached pronoun 'its' (referring to a feminine thing). It points to the space below or underneath a thing.
11.grammar: A location noun ('underneath') with the attached pronoun '-hā' ('its/her'), referring to a feminine noun. The -i ending is the genitive case, normally triggered here because words of place like 'under' commonly follow a preposition such as 'from' (min taḥti = 'from beneath').

12.meaning: 'The rivers / the streams' — the definite plural of a word for a flowing river or watercourse. It denotes large, running channels of water.
12.grammar: A definite plural noun ('the rivers'). The -u ending is the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence — the doer of the verb or the thing being described.

13.meaning: They are adorned, decorated, or made to wear ornaments — the passive sense of being beautified with jewelry.
13.grammar: A present-tense passive verb, third-person masculine plural ('they are adorned'). The yu- prefix with the intensive doubled middle letter signals a Form II passive (to have ornaments richly applied to one). The -awna ending marks the masculine plural in the indicative mood (a plain statement of ongoing/future fact).

14.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
14.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

15.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
15.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
15.root: — (preposition)

16.meaning: Bracelets, armlets — 'asāwir' is the plural of 'siwār', the band worn around the wrist or arm.
16.grammar: A plural noun of a special pattern (a 'diptote') that resists nunation; its -a ending serves as the accusative, typically marking it as the direct object (the thing received or acted upon). This plural shape ordinarily also stands in for the genitive without taking nunation.

17.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
17.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

18.meaning: Gold — the precious yellow metal 'dhahab'.
18.grammar: An indefinite noun with the -in ending: the genitive case with nunation. This case commonly links the word to a preceding noun in an 'of' relationship (e.g. 'bracelets of gold') or follows a preposition.

19.meaning: And pearls — the precious gems produced inside oysters, used in descriptions of the adornments and luxuries of Paradise.
19.grammar: Luʾluʾ is the Arabic word for pearl. The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥa) marks the accusative case indefinitely — used when the noun is the object of a verb or follows certain particles. The doubled fatḥa (tanwīn) also signals indefiniteness.

20.meaning: And their garments / clothing — referring to what they wear; the dress or attire belonging to them.
20.grammar: Libās is a noun meaning 'clothing, garment, attire'. The attached pronoun hum makes it 'their garments'. The -u ending on libāsu is the nominative case (ḍamma), indicating that the noun is the subject of its clause. The possessive pronoun hum also causes the noun to be considered definite (as a genitive construct: 'the garments of them').
20.root: ل-ب-س (l-b-s) — to wear, to clothe; garment, covering

21.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
21.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

22.meaning: Silk — the fine, smooth, lustrous fabric woven from silkworm thread, mentioned among the magnificent garments of the inhabitants of Paradise.
22.grammar: Ḥarīr is a simple noun on the faʿīl pattern. The -un ending is the indefinite nominative (tanwīn ḍamma), used here as a predicate ('their garments will be silk') — when a noun is the predicate of an equational sentence it typically takes the nominative case.
22.root: ح-ر-ر (ḥ-r-r) — heat, freedom; the root also underlies ḥarīr (silk), likely from its smooth, flowing quality

1.meaning: And they were guided — guidance was granted to them; the passive leaves the Guide unnamed, pointing to guidance as a gift received.
1.grammar: A passive past-tense verb: the u-vowel pattern (hudū rather than hadaw) marks the passive — 'they were guided' rather than 'they guided'. The -ū ending means 'they' (masculine plural), a completed action experienced by a group. Wa- prefixes 'and'.

2.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
2.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

3.meaning: An adjective/noun meaning 'the good', 'the wholesome', or 'the pure' — that which is pleasant, clean, lawful, and agreeable; the opposite of foul or corrupt.
3.grammar: A definite adjective ('the good/wholesome') on the intensive 'fayyil' pattern, in which a weak middle root letter (yāʾ) is doubled — shown by the shadda on the yāʾ of 'ṭayyib'. It carries the definite article 'al-' (whose 'l' assimilates into the following emphatic 'ṭ', marked by the doubling of that letter) and the genitive '-i' ending. The genitive case typically follows a preposition or links the word to a preceding genitive noun.
3.root: ط-ي-ب (ṭ-y-b) — to be good, pleasant, wholesome, pure

4.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
4.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

5.meaning: Speech, an utterance, a statement, or a saying — that which is said. It denotes the act or content of speaking.
5.grammar: A definite noun ('the speech'). The -i ending is the genitive case: it typically links the word to a preceding noun in an 'of …' relationship or follows a preposition.

6.meaning: And they were guided — guidance was granted to them; the passive leaves the Guide unnamed, pointing to guidance as a gift received.
6.grammar: A passive past-tense verb: the u-vowel pattern (hudū rather than hadaw) marks the passive — 'they were guided' rather than 'they guided'. The -ū ending means 'they' (masculine plural), a completed action experienced by a group. Wa- prefixes 'and'.

7.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
7.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

8.meaning: A path, road, or way. It is frequently used for a clear, broad highway, and figuratively for the straight way of right guidance and conduct.
8.grammar: A masculine noun in the genitive case, shown by the -i ending. The genitive typically means the word is linked to a following noun ('the path OF …') or follows a preposition.

9.meaning: The Praiseworthy, the One deserving of all praise. As a divine attribute it denotes the One who is intrinsically worthy of praise whether or not anyone praises Him; it can also carry the sense of 'ever-praised.'
9.grammar: A noun/adjective in the intensive paradigm (carrying a deep, settled quality), made definite by al- ('the'). The -i ending is genitive, which usually means it is linked to a preceding noun or follows a preposition.

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
3.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

4.meaning: And they bar / turn (others) away — a present-tense verb of a group obstructing, hindering, or diverting people from a path or course.
4.grammar: A plain (form I) present-tense verb. The ya- prefix with the -ūna ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they') and the -ūna specifically signals the indicative mood — a real, ongoing or habitual action ('they hinder / keep turning away').

5.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on behalf of,' 'for,' 'about,' or 'away from.' It often conveys removing a burden from someone or acting in their place.

parts.en: on behalf of / for / away from

5.grammar: A preposition (a linking particle). It governs the noun that follows it, putting that noun into the genitive case. It does not change form.

6.meaning: 'path, way, road' — a route or course; figuratively a cause or way of life one travels along. In construct ('the way OF ...').
6.grammar: A singular noun with the '-i' (genitive) ending, which typically links it to a following noun ('the way OF ...') or follows a preposition. It marks the word as connected to or possessed by what comes after.

7.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
7.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

8.meaning: And the place of prostration / the mosque — a site set aside for bowing down in worship of Allah.
8.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and' and al- means 'the'. The stem is a 'place noun' (mafʿil pattern) naming where the act of prostration happens. The final -i is genitive: it typically links the word to a following noun ('… of …') or follows a preposition or oath particle.

9.meaning: The sacred, inviolable, forbidden; that which is set apart and protected, whose violation is prohibited out of reverence. Describes something hallowed.
9.grammar: An adjective on the form faʿāl ('sacred/forbidden'), prefixed with al- ('the'). The final -i ending is the genitive case; an adjective takes the same case as the noun it describes, so this -i matches a preceding genitive noun ('the … sacred').
9.root: ح-ر-م (ḥ-r-m) — being forbidden, sacred, set apart, inviolable

10.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
10.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

11.meaning: 'We made him / appointed him / rendered him so.' The verb of making or setting into a state (jaʿala), with attached pronouns for the subject 'we' and the object 'him.'
11.grammar: A past-tense verb with the subject ending -nā ('we,' a completed act by a plural or majestic 'we') and the attached object -hu ('him/it'). It denotes making, placing, or rendering the object into some state.
11.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, place, render, appoint

12.meaning: To the people, for mankind — addressed or directed toward human beings in general; 'an-nās' is the collective word for 'people, humankind'.
12.grammar: The preposition 'li-' (to/for) joined to 'an-nās' (the people); the article's 'a' drops in pronunciation and its 'l' assimilates into the noun's 'n' (shown by the doubling). The -i ending is the genitive case, required because the word follows the preposition 'li-'. 'nās' is a collective noun for humankind with no singular of its own root form.

13.meaning: Equal / alike — the same for both sides, with no difference of standing between them.
13.grammar: A noun meaning 'equality, sameness' often used adjectivally. The -an ending is accusative plus tanwīn (indefinite): the accusative is the case used for objects of verbs and for words describing the state or manner in which something is done ('as equals, equally').

14.meaning: The one who stays in devotion / the resident — an active participle of ʿakafa, to remain clinging devotedly to a place; hence one settled at a sacred place.
14.grammar: An active participle on the pattern CāCiC, 'one who does' the action — here 'one who stays/devotes himself'. Made definite by l- 'the'. The -u ending is nominative, the case of the subject or the thing under discussion.
14.root: ع-ك-ف (ʿ-k-f) — to cling to, remain devotedly at

15.meaning: 'In it / in him' — the preposition 'in, inside, within' joined to a pronoun referring to a single masculine or neuter thing. It locates something inside or as part of that referent.
15.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The pronoun -hi refers to one masculine (or grammatically masculine) thing and stands as the object of the preposition; its vowel is -i because attached pronouns take that shape after the long -i of fi. Together they answer 'in what?' or 'in whom?'.

16.meaning: And the visitor from outside — the desert-dweller or one who comes in from the open country; an active participle of badā, 'to appear, be out in the open'.
16.grammar: An active participle ('one who is out in the open') from a root ending in a weak letter; the full form is al-bādī with a long ī, as such nouns normally keep their ī when definite (like al-qāḍī 'the judge'). This particular word, however, is traditionally written and recited without the final yāʾ — a pausal-style spelling preserved in the received Qur'anic text for this word — leaving the short -i heard at the end. Wa- prefixes 'and', l- is 'the'.
16.root: ب-د-و (b-d-w) — to appear, be out in the open desert

17.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
17.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

18.meaning: 'He wants / intends / desires' — to will or aim at something, present tense.
18.grammar: A present-tense verb (causative form, here showing the yu- prefix typical of that pattern), third-person masculine singular, 'he wants'. The vowelless (sukūn) final consonant marks the jussive (majzūm) mood used after conditional particles, giving a conditional 'if he wants'.

19.meaning: 'In it / in him' — the preposition 'in, inside, within' joined to a pronoun referring to a single masculine or neuter thing. It locates something inside or as part of that referent.
19.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The pronoun -hi refers to one masculine (or grammatically masculine) thing and stands as the object of the preposition; its vowel is -i because attached pronouns take that shape after the long -i of fi. Together they answer 'in what?' or 'in whom?'.

20.meaning: With deviation — ilḥād is a swerving away from the straight course into wrong; the same root gives 'laḥd', the side-niche of a grave, dug off the straight line.
20.grammar: The preposition bi- 'with/by' attached to a Form IV verbal noun ('the act of deviating'). The -in ending is genitive plus tanwīn: the genitive is required after a preposition like bi-, and the -n marks indefiniteness ('any deviation').
20.root: ل-ح-د (l-ḥ-d) — to incline away, deviate from the straight

21.meaning: 'with wrongdoing / with injustice' — with putting things out of their right place: injustice, oppression, or wrong, governed by a preceding preposition.
21.grammar: The preposition bi- ('with') attached to the noun 'wrongdoing.' The ending -in is the genitive with indefinite 'nunation' ('with some wrong'); the genitive case is required after a preposition.
21.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — to wrong, oppress, put out of place; darkness

22.meaning: We make him taste — a causative verb of tasting used for experience: to cause someone to feel and undergo something directly.
22.grammar: A Form IV causative verb: 'taste' becomes 'make (someone) taste'. The nu- prefix means 'we'. The stem is in the shortened (jussive) form — the long ī of nudhīqu is dropped — a form that typically appears in the result-clause of a condition ('whoever…, We will make him taste…'). The suffix -hu is the attached object pronoun 'him'.

23.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
23.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

24.meaning: A punishment / torment — painful chastisement or suffering imposed as a penalty. The word names the punishment itself, stated indefinitely ('a punishment').
24.grammar: A noun, 'punishment/torment'. The final -in (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a punishment') and genitive in case — the form used after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of a punishment').

25.meaning: Painful / agonizing: causing intense pain; said of something that grieves and torments deeply. An intensive adjective, so 'sorely painful'. Indefinite ('a painful …').
25.grammar: An indefinite adjective on an intensive pattern (conveying 'deeply/sorely painful'). The ending -in shows both indefiniteness (the final -n, nunation: 'a painful one') and the genitive case (the -i vowel), the case that an adjective takes to match a genitive noun it describes or that follows a preposition.

1.meaning: 'And when / and at the time when' — the connective 'and' joined to a word that points to a past moment or circumstance ('when'), introducing the recollection of an event or situation.
1.grammar: A connective particle plus a time-word. The wa- prefix means 'and'. 'Idh' is an invariable adverb pointing to a definite time in the past ('when, at the moment that'); it has no case ending and typically introduces a clause recalling a past event.

2.meaning: We settled / established (someone in a place) — a verb meaning to give a people a dwelling, to lodge or station them in a secure abode.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb. The intensive (form II) stem bawwa'a conveys causing to dwell or settling someone in. The suffix -nā is the first-person plural subject attached to a past verb, meaning 'we'. So: 'we settled / we gave a dwelling'.
2.root: ب-و-أ (b-w-ʾ) — to take up a dwelling, to settle, abode

3.meaning: For Ibrahim — the prophet Ibrahim (Abraham), preceded by the preposition 'for/to'.

parts.en: genitive ending of a diptote name

3.grammar: The preposition li- 'for/to' attached to a proper name. A preposition puts the following word in the genitive, but foreign proper names like Ibrāhīm belong to a class (diptotes) that cannot take the usual genitive -i; they show the genitive with -a instead — which is exactly the ending heard here.

4.meaning: Place, position, location — the spot or stead occupied by something. In phrases it functions like 'in place of' or 'instead of', marking where one thing stands relative to another.
4.grammar: A noun with the accusative -a ending. This ending here signals an adverbial sense of place ('in the place of') or marks it as a direct object; it commonly leads into a following noun in a possessive link ('the place OF …').
4.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be (the place where something 'is')

5.meaning: Al-bayt — the house, dwelling, or home; a place of residence or a building set apart, often used for a household or a place of worship.
5.grammar: A definite noun. The final -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a following noun ('… of …') or follows a preposition or oath particle. The word denotes a house, dwelling, or set-apart sacred building.
5.root: ب-ي-ت (b-y-t) — to spend the night; house, dwelling

6.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
6.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

7.meaning: 'Not' — a particle of negation. Depending on context it denies a present fact, forbids an action, or rules something out ('do not / there is no').
7.grammar: A negating particle, 'not / no'. It is used to deny or prohibit — negating present-tense statements, expressing 'there is no...', or, with a command form, forbidding an action ('do not...').

8.meaning: associate partners (with Allah)
8.grammar: verb, imperfect jussive (مجزوم), Form IV (أَشْرَكَ), 2nd person masculine singular, used after negative lā (لَا)
8.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — to associate, to be a partner, to commit shirk

9.meaning: 'In me / with me.' A preposition fused with the first-person singular pronoun, expressing attachment, belief, or trust directed toward the speaker ('me').
9.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') joined to the attached pronoun -ī ('me'). The -ī here is the first-person singular object that always follows a preposition or noun; it does not change for case. Combined sense: 'in me' or 'with me.'

10.meaning: A thing; something or anything. With a negation it commonly amounts to 'nothing at all.'
10.grammar: A singular masculine noun, indefinite ('a thing'). The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative, often used here as an object or an adverbial 'in any respect / at all.'

11.meaning: And purify! — a command to cleanse thoroughly; the intensive verb form implies making something completely pure.
11.grammar: A Form II verb (doubled middle letter), which adds intensity or thoroughness: not just 'be pure' but 'make thoroughly pure'. It is an imperative addressed to one person ('you: purify!'), and like all such commands it ends with no vowel at all (a sukūn) — which is why the transliteration ends flat on -ir with no case vowel. Wa- prefixes 'and'.

12.meaning: My house, my dwelling. 'Bayt' (house/abode) with the first-person possessive, making it 'my house.'
12.grammar: A noun with the first-person singular possessive pronoun 'my,' which here appears in the fuller form -iya (the connecting vowel -i plus -ya). This -iya ('my') marks possession regardless of the noun's grammatical role in the sentence.
12.root: ب-ي-ت (b-y-t) — to spend the night, dwell; a house

13.meaning: Those who circle around (a sacred object) on foot; the active participle for people who perform a circuit, especially the ritual going-around of the Kaʿba (ṭawāf). In a broader sense it can name those who go about or move around something.
13.grammar: A sound masculine plural active participle carried by the preposition li- ('for/to'). The -īna ending is the oblique (accusative/genitive) form of the masculine plural; following a preposition it is genitive, marking the group as the object of 'for'. The form denotes ongoing doers of the action 'to circle around'.
13.root: ط-و-ف (ṭ-w-f) — to go around, circle, circumambulate

14.meaning: And those who stand — active participle of qāma 'to stand'; ones standing, especially standing upright in prayer.
14.grammar: An active participle ('one who stands') made plural with the sound masculine plural ending -īna. This -īna form is the shape the plural takes in the accusative and genitive cases — used for objects of verbs, after prepositions, or when coordinated with other words in those cases (the subject form would be -ūna). Wa- 'and' plus l- 'the' complete the word.
14.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise, be upright

15.meaning: Those who bow; the plural for worshippers performing rukūʿ, the bowing of the body in prayer. It conveys humble bending before Allah.
15.grammar: Conjunction wa- ('and') plus a definite broken (irregular) plural noun of the pattern fuʿʿal, which names a group of doers ('bowers'). The final -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a following noun ('… of …') or follows a preposition or oath particle.
15.root: ر-ك-ع (r-k-ʿ) — to bow down (in prayer)

16.meaning: Those who prostrate, or the act of prostration itself; relating to sujūd, placing the forehead on the ground in submission to Allah. The form can name a group of prostrating worshippers or the state of prostration.
16.grammar: A definite noun of the pattern fuʿūl, used as a verbal noun ('prostration') and also as a plural for those prostrating. The final -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a following noun ('… of …') or follows a preposition or oath particle.
16.root: س-ج-د (s-j-d) — to prostrate, bow the forehead to the ground

1.meaning: And proclaim aloud — make a public announcement so that all may hear. The verb carries the sense of calling out openly, the same root that gives adhān, the call to prayer.
1.grammar: A command form (imperative) addressed to one man: 'proclaim!'. It is an intensive verb pattern (Form II, with the doubled middle letter) meaning to make something loudly and widely known, not merely to say it. The bare ending with no final vowel is the normal mark of a command.
1.root: أ-ذ-ن (ʾ-dh-n) — the ear; hearing, announcing, giving notice

2.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
2.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

3.meaning: Humankind, people, mankind — the collective of human beings.
3.grammar: A collective noun ('people, mankind') carrying the definite article al- ('the'); the 'l' of the article assimilates into the following 'n', doubling it (al-nās → an-nās). The genitive ending -i marks the word as governed by a preposition or as the second term of a possessive.
3.root: ء-ن-س (ʾ-n-s) — humankind, sociability, familiarity; the word for 'people' is most commonly traced to this root (related to insān, 'human being')

4.meaning: The Ḥajj — the great Pilgrimage to the Sacred House at Makkah. The word literally means setting out toward a revered destination with firm intent; with bi- it means '(proclaim) the Pilgrimage'.
4.grammar: The preposition bi- ('with/of') attaches to the front, and every noun after a preposition takes the genitive -i ending — that is exactly what the final -i marks. The al- ('the') makes it definite: the well-known Pilgrimage, not just any journey.
4.root: ح-ج-ج (ḥ-j-j) — heading purposefully to a venerated place; pilgrimage

5.meaning: A verb meaning 'they come to you' — an act of approaching or arriving at a second person (masculine singular), with the 'you' built into the word as the goal of the coming.
5.grammar: A present/imperfect verb. The ya-…-ū frame marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). The attached -ka is a pronoun meaning 'you' (one male) and serves as the goal/object of the coming. The verb stands in the jussive (the mood after a conditional particle), where the final 'n' of the indicative plural ending -ūna drops, leaving just -ū.

6.meaning: Men — the plural of 'man' (an adult male); also carries the sense of menfolk as distinct from women.
6.grammar: A plural noun in the indefinite accusative, marked by the -an ending (tanwīn fatḥa). This ending typically signals the word is a direct object, or names something brought about/scattered ('[He made/produced] men…').

7.meaning: A compound, 'and upon / and on / and against' — the connector 'and' joined to the preposition ʿalā ('on, over, against'). It adds a further thing onto which something rests or against which it bears.
7.grammar: The prefix wa- is the connective 'and', joining what follows to what came before. ʿalā is an indeclinable preposition that puts the following noun in the genitive case and signals 'on, over, or upon' something.

8.meaning: 'every,' 'each,' or 'all' — a word expressing totality or completeness. It indicates the entirety of something: when joined to a singular indefinite noun it means 'every (single) one,' and when joined to a definite noun it can mean 'all of' or 'the whole of.'
8.grammar: A noun of totality. The final '-i' ending is genitive (the 'of/possession' case): it marks the word as governed by a preceding preposition or as the first term of a possessive link to a following noun, so it typically reads 'of every…' or 'every…' leading into what follows.

9.meaning: A lean, gaunt riding camel — one grown thin from the hardship of long travel. The word evokes a mount worn slender by crossing great distances.
9.grammar: An active-participle shape ('one that is lean'). The -in ending is the genitive with nunation: the doubled vowel sound marks the word as indefinite ('a lean camel', any such camel), and the i-vowel shows it follows a preposition or is linked to another word by 'of'.
9.root: ض-م-ر (ḍ-m-r) — leanness, slenderness, being trimmed down

10.meaning: 'They (females) come to' / 'they commit / perpetrate' — from the verb meaning 'to come', here in the sense of bringing about or committing an act. The subject is a group of females.
10.grammar: A present-tense verb with a feminine-plural subject ('they [women] do/commit'). The -na ending here is the subject marker for a group of females (and is a fixed part of the feminine-plural verb, so the verb's mood does not change this ending). The core sense is 'to come (to)', extended to 'commit/perpetrate' an act.
10.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come, arrive, bring about

11.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
11.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

12.meaning: 'every,' 'each,' or 'all' — a word expressing totality or completeness. It indicates the entirety of something: when joined to a singular indefinite noun it means 'every (single) one,' and when joined to a definite noun it can mean 'all of' or 'the whole of.'
12.grammar: A noun of totality. The final '-i' ending is genitive (the 'of/possession' case): it marks the word as governed by a preceding preposition or as the first term of a possessive link to a following noun, so it typically reads 'of every…' or 'every…' leading into what follows.

13.meaning: A wide mountain pass or deep road between hills — a broad path cut through high ground, by extension any far-stretching route.
13.grammar: A simple noun. The -in ending combines two signals: the nunation (the 'n' sound) marks it as indefinite ('a pass', any pass), and the i-vowel is the genitive case, used after prepositions or in an 'of'-link with another noun.
13.root: ف-ج-ج (f-j-j) — a broad way between two mountains; wide opening

14.meaning: Deep — and, of a road or journey, far and remote: stretching so far it feels 'deep' in distance.
14.grammar: An adjective on the faʿīl pattern (like karīm 'generous'), describing an inherent quality. Adjectives copy the case of the noun they describe, so its -in ending — indefinite genitive — matches a preceding indefinite genitive noun.

1.meaning: So that they may witness — be personally present at and experience for themselves. The verb means both to see with one's own eyes and to attend in person.
1.grammar: The li- prefix means 'in order that' and it changes the verb's mood: the normal plural ending -ūna loses its final -na, leaving just -ū. So the -ū ending means 'they (a group of men)', and the missing -na is the visible sign of a purpose clause ('so that they may…').

2.meaning: Benefits, advantages, useful things — the plural of manfaʿah, anything from which good and profit are drawn, whether worldly or spiritual.
2.grammar: A 'broken' plural (the inside of the word changes rather than adding a suffix): manfaʿah becomes manāfiʿ. This plural pattern is a diptote — it never takes nunation, and it shows a single -a vowel for both the object case and the 'of'-case. So the -a ending simply marks its case without the usual indefinite 'n' sound.

3.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
3.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

4.meaning: And that they may remember and mention — invoke by name. Dhikr covers both inward remembrance of Allah and speaking His name aloud.
4.grammar: The -ū ending means 'they (a group of men)'. The full plural ending would be -ūna; the dropped -na shows the verb is in a dependent mood, the form used when a verb continues a 'so that…' purpose chain begun by an earlier li-. The wa- simply joins it to that chain: 'and (that they may) remember'.

5.meaning: Name — the word or designation by which someone or something is called; in worship, the invoking of a name (especially Allah's) over an act.
5.grammar: A noun ('ism,' 'name'). The final '-a' (fatḥa) is the accusative case, the form typically used when the word is the direct object of a verb — the thing being acted upon.
5.root: س-م-و (s-m-w) — height, loftiness; the source of 'ism' (name)

6.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
6.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

7.meaning: The preposition 'in / within / during.' It places something inside a container, period, place, or matter.
7.grammar: A preposition. It governs the noun that follows, putting it in the genitive case and situating something inside it — in space, in time ('during'), or in a circumstance.

8.meaning: Days — the plural of 'day,' periods of daylight or twenty-four-hour spans.
8.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of yawm ('day'). The ending -in (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('days') and in the genitive case, the form used in a possessive link ('… of days') or after a preposition.

9.meaning: Known, fixed, appointed — things that are definitely specified. Describing days, it means days that are set and well-known in advance.
9.grammar: A passive participle ('that which is known') on the maf'ūl pattern, with the sound feminine plural -āt. This -āt plural never takes the -a vowel: it uses -i(n) for both the object case and the 'of'-case, so the -in here is that shared ending plus nunation marking indefiniteness.

10.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
10.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

11.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
11.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

12.meaning: He provided them, He gave them sustenance — rizq is provision in the widest sense: food, livelihood, every good thing Allah supplies.
12.grammar: A past-tense verb: the final -a of razaqa marks 'he' (third person masculine singular) in the perfect tense — a completed act of providing. The attached pronoun -hum ('them') is the direct object, so the one word says 'he provided them'.

13.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
13.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

14.meaning: Beast, grazing animal — literally 'the mute one', an animal that cannot speak; used of cattle and livestock.
14.grammar: A feminine noun (the tāʾ marbūṭah ending is pronounced -t when another word follows). The -i ending is the genitive: it typically links the word to a neighbouring noun in an 'of'-relationship or follows a preposition. Having no al- and no nunation, it stands in a construct chain — 'the beast of…'.
14.root: ب-ه-م (b-h-m) — being mute, indistinct; hence dumb animals

15.meaning: 'the grazing livestock / cattle' — a collective term for domesticated herd animals such as camels, cattle, sheep, and goats, valued as wealth and as a provision.
15.grammar: A definite noun ('the …') with the -i (genitive) ending, which typically links it to a preceding noun in a possessive 'of …' relationship or follows a preposition. It is itself a plural of naʿam (livestock).
15.root: ن-ع-م (n-ʿ-m) — softness, ease; grazing livestock, bounty/blessing

16.meaning: 'Then eat!' — a command to a group to eat, joined by 'then / so', which links it as a following or resulting step.
16.grammar: An imperative (command) verb prefixed with fa- 'then/so', which marks sequence or consequence ('and then…', 'so…'). The -ū ending aims the command at a group ('you all, eat!'). This verb drops its original first root letter, so the stem is just kul-. The silent alif after the wāw spells the plural ending.

17.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'min' ('from / out of / some of') joined to the pronoun 'it' (feminine). Together: 'from it / out of it / of it,' indicating a source or a portion taken from a feminine thing.
17.grammar: A preposition 'min' with the attached pronoun '-hā' ('it/her'), referring to a feminine noun. 'Min' indicates origin, source, or a part taken from a whole; the attached pronoun is in the object form required after a preposition.

18.meaning: And feed — give food to, cause someone to eat. A command of generosity: put food into the hands of another.
18.grammar: A plural command: the a- prefix with this verb pattern (Form IV, the causative) turns 'eat' into 'make eat, feed', and the -ū ending addresses a group — 'you all, feed!'. Wa- joins it to a preceding command.

19.meaning: The one in misery, the hard-pressed — a person crushed by distress and want, from the same root as ba's, hardship.
19.grammar: An active participle ('one who is in hardship') made definite by al- 'the'. The final -a is the accusative case, the ending a noun takes when it is the direct object — the one receiving the action of a verb such as giving or feeding.
19.root: ب-أ-س (b-ʾ-s) — hardship, misery, distress; also might

20.meaning: The poor, the needy — faqīr literally suggests one whose 'backbone is broken' by need; a person lacking the means to meet his needs.
20.grammar: An adjective-noun on the faʿīl pattern with al- 'the'. Its -a ending is the accusative case, marking a direct object; when it follows another accusative noun it acts as its description, agreeing with it in case ('the wretched, the poor').
20.root: ف-ق-ر (f-q-r) — poverty, need; the spine (bent by want)

1.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
1.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

2.meaning: Then let them bring to an end / carry out fully — the verb qaḍā means to complete, settle, and discharge something due.
2.grammar: The l- prefix is the 'lām of command': attached to a they-form verb it turns a statement into an order about a third party — 'let them…'. This command particle puts the verb in the shortened (jussive) mood, so the plural ending -ūna drops its -na, leaving -ū ('they').

3.meaning: Their tafath — the accumulated untidiness of the body during the pilgrim's consecrated state: unkempt hair, uncut nails, general dishevelment, ended by the rites of release.
3.grammar: A noun with the possessive pronoun -hum ('their') attached. The -a before the pronoun is the accusative case ending, the mark of a direct object — the thing acted upon by a verb.

4.meaning: And let them fulfil — pay in full, keep completely. The verb awfā means to discharge an obligation without falling short.
4.grammar: Wa- 'and' plus the lām of command: 'and let them…'. The command particle shortens the verb into the jussive mood, so the plural -ūna ending loses its -na, leaving -ū meaning 'they'. The verb itself is the causative pattern (Form IV) of the root: 'to give something its full due'.
4.root: و-ف-ي (w-f-y) — fulfilling, completing, giving in full

5.meaning: Their vows — nudhūr, plural of nadhr: a voluntary pledge a person binds upon himself for Allah's sake, which then becomes obligatory.
5.grammar: A broken plural ('vow' nadhr becomes 'vows' nudhūr by internal vowel change) with the possessive -hum ('their'). The -a before the pronoun is the accusative ending, marking the word as the direct object of a verb.

6.meaning: And let them go around, circle — ṭawāf, the rite of walking in circuits around something; the intensive form suggests doing so repeatedly and devotedly.
6.grammar: Wa- 'and' plus the lām of command ('let them…'). The verb is a reflexive-intensive pattern (Form V, originally yataṭawwafū, with the ta- absorbed into the ṭ) — circling again and again. The command particle drops the -na of the plural ending, leaving -ū, 'they'.
6.root: ط-و-ف (ṭ-w-f) — going around, circling, making circuits

7.meaning: Around the House — al-Bayt, 'the House', is the honoured title of the Kaʿbah, the House of Allah; with bi- it means '(circle) around the House'.
7.grammar: The preposition bi- attaches to the front (with verbs of circling it means 'around'), and every noun governed by a preposition takes the genitive -i ending — that is what the final -i marks. Al- makes it definite: the one well-known House.
7.root: ب-ي-ت (b-y-t) — house, dwelling; passing the night

8.meaning: The Ancient — ʿatīq means old and venerable, but also noble and set free; as a title of the Kaʿbah it carries both senses: the most ancient sanctuary, and one freed from the grip of tyrants.
8.grammar: An adjective with al- 'the'. Adjectives mirror the case of the noun they describe, so its genitive -i ending matches a preceding genitive noun — the -i is the case that follows prepositions or an 'of'-link.
8.root: ع-ت-ق (ʿ-t-q) — being ancient; being freed; nobility

1.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
1.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

2.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
2.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

3.meaning: He honours, magnifies, holds in reverence — treats something as ʿaẓīm, great, giving it the weight and veneration it deserves.
3.grammar: Present-tense verb: the yu- prefix means 'he'. The doubled middle letter is the intensive pattern (Form II): 'to make great, treat as great'. The bare ending with no final vowel (sukūn) is the shortened jussive mood — the form a verb takes inside an 'if/whoever…' conditional sentence or after a command particle.

4.meaning: The sacred things (of) — ḥurumāt, plural of ḥurmah: everything Allah has declared inviolable, whose sanctity must not be violated — sacred rites, places, months, and limits.
4.grammar: A sound feminine plural (-āt). This plural type never takes the -a vowel: the single -i ending serves for both the object case and the 'of'-case. Bearing no al- and no nunation, it stands as the first word of an 'of'-chain: 'the sacred things of…'.

5.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
5.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

6.meaning: A two-part phrase: the connector 'then / so' plus the standalone pronoun 'he / it,' used to point back and resume with 'then he…' or 'so it…'
6.grammar: The connector 'fa' ('then/so') plus the detached subject pronoun 'huwa' ('he/it'), 3rd-person masculine singular. Both are indeclinable, with no case ending; the pronoun typically begins or emphasizes a statement about 'he/it.'

7.meaning: 'Better / best; good' — an adjective of comparison meaning more good, preferable, or superior. It also serves broadly for 'goodness' and that which is good and beneficial.
7.grammar: A noun/adjective bearing the ending -un (nunation): the doubled-u 'n' sound marks the word as both indefinite ('a/an', no 'the') and nominative — the case used for the subject of a sentence or the predicate that describes it.
7.root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r) — good, goodness, that which is choice and beneficial

8.meaning: A two-part phrase 'for Him' or 'to Him belongs,' expressing possession, ownership, or that something is due to one masculine being.
8.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('for/to/belonging to') with its vowel shifted to 'la-' before the pronoun. The attached -hu means 'Him', so the whole means 'for Him' or 'His'; the preposition signals possession or that something is owed or directed to that person.

9.meaning: 'With / in the presence of / near' — an adverb of place and relation meaning at, by, in the sight or estimation of someone. It indicates nearness, possession, or what holds in someone's view (as in 'with Allah' = in His sight).
9.grammar: An adverb of place that is always followed by a noun it relates to. It carries a fixed -a ending; this accusative-type vowel is characteristic of such adverbs of place and shows the word is functioning to locate something ('at, near, in the presence of').

10.meaning: His Lord; the Master, Owner, Sustainer, and Nurturer who creates, provides for, and brings each thing to its completion. Rabb conveys ownership, authority, and loving care all at once.
10.grammar: A noun with the attached pronoun -hi meaning 'his.' The -i on the stem is the genitive ending, the case typically used after a preposition or to link a noun to a preceding one ('… OF …'); the pronoun then shifts to -hi to harmonize with that -i vowel, giving 'of his Lord / his Lord's.'
10.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master; lordship and ownership

11.meaning: And it has been made lawful — declared ḥalāl, permitted. The passive leaves the doer unnamed because the One who permits is Allah alone.
11.grammar: A past-tense passive verb: the u-i vowel pattern (uḥillat rather than aḥallat) is the classic passive shape, 'was made lawful' — the action is stated without naming its doer. The final -t marks a feminine subject ('it/she'), agreeing with a feminine or plural noun. Wa- is simply 'and'.

12.meaning: 'for you,' 'to you,' 'for your benefit' — the preposition 'for/to' joined to 'you (plural).' It marks the party for whose sake, benefit, or possession something is done or given.
12.grammar: A preposition ('for/to') with the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you, plural'). Such prepositions assign a benefit, purpose, or recipient. The pronoun's vowel appears as '-u' (kumu) to ease pronunciation when a word follows.

13.meaning: Grazing livestock — camels, cattle, sheep and goats as a class of domestic animals given for human benefit. The plural of naʿam, from a root suggesting ease and blessing, so the word itself carries the sense of animals as a provision and comfort.
13.grammar: A plural noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The final -u is the nominative case ending: it typically marks the word as the subject of a sentence, or the one being talked about ('the livestock ARE/DO …').

14.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
14.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

15.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
15.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

16.meaning: It is recited / read aloud — a passage of revelation is being conveyed by being read out.
16.grammar: Present-tense passive verb, third-person masculine singular ('it is being recited'). The yu- prefix with the internal vowel pattern marks the passive (no doer named), and the final weak -ā shows it derives from a root ending in a weak letter; it conveys an ongoing action done to the subject.
16.root: ت-ل-و (t-l-w) — to recite, read aloud, follow

17.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
17.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.

18.meaning: 'So shun / keep well away from' — a plural command to avoid something. The verb form (Form VIII of the root for 'side') literally pictures putting a thing to one side, deliberately steering clear of it, not merely refraining once.
18.grammar: An imperative (command) verb. The fa- prefix means 'so/therefore', drawing a consequence. The -ū ending marks the command as addressed to a group: 'you all, avoid!'. Form VIII of the root adds the sense of doing it deliberately for oneself.
18.root: ج-ن-ب (j-n-b) — side; to put at a distance

19.meaning: A noun meaning 'filth', 'defilement', or 'abomination' — that which is impure, foul, or repugnant, whether physically unclean or spiritually corrupting.
19.grammar: A definite noun with the article al- (its 'l' assimilated into the following 'r', producing 'r-rijs'). The -a (accusative) ending typically marks it as the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon).

20.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
20.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

21.meaning: The idols — carved images or objects set up and worshipped besides Allah. Awthān is the plural of wathan, an idol of stone, wood, or any fashioned material.
21.grammar: A plural noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The final -i is the genitive case ending: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the idols') or shows it follows a preposition such as min ('from').

22.meaning: And avoid / shun! — a command to a group to keep away from, steer clear of, and stay on one side away from something; to give it a wide berth.
22.grammar: A command (imperative) to a group, joined by 'and'. The -ū ending directs the order at a masculine plural 'you' ('you all, avoid!'). The initial helping vowel (i-) appears because the stem would otherwise begin with a consonant cluster. Form VIII here conveys deliberately keeping oneself away.
22.root: ج-ن-ب (j-n-b) — side, flank; to keep to one side of, avoid

23.meaning: The saying, statement, or utterance — speech that is spoken; a word, remark, or what someone says.
23.grammar: A noun, 'saying/speech.' The final -a ending is the accusative case, which commonly marks the noun as the direct object — the thing the verb acts upon (e.g., what is heard, said, or known). This form names the act or product of speaking.
23.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak; an utterance

24.meaning: Falsehood — speech or testimony that swerves from the truth: lying, slander, false witness. The root sense is deviation, inclining away from what is straight, so zūr is crookedness put into words.
24.grammar: A noun with the definite article; before the 'sun letter' z the l of al- assimilates, so it is pronounced az-zūr. The final -i is the genitive case ending: it typically ties the word to a preceding noun ('… OF falsehood') or follows a preposition.

1.meaning: Plural of ḥanīf: people who incline away from every false object of worship toward pure devotion to Allah alone — upright monotheists by natural bent, not by mere convention.
1.grammar: A plural noun of a pattern that takes only a single vowel for case (a 'diptote'). The final -a here is the accusative ending; on words like this it typically marks a state or condition — describing HOW someone is while doing something ('… being upright ones').
1.root: ح-ن-ف (ḥ-n-f) — to incline away (from falsehood toward truth)

2.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'li-' meaning 'to', 'for', or 'belonging to', attached to the name 'Allah'. It conveys 'to Allah' or 'for Allah'.
2.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('to/for') pulls the following noun into the genitive case, which is why 'Allah' ends in '-i' (llāhi). The '-i' ending is the regular result of a noun governed by a preposition.

3.meaning: 'Other than / different from / not'. A noun used to express difference or negation — 'something other than X', and so 'not-X'. It functions to exclude or contrast with what follows.
3.grammar: A noun of difference/exception. The -a ending marks the accusative case, the form it takes when it serves as a direct object or as a descriptive substitute standing in an object position; it governs a following noun in the genitive ('other than …'). That it takes case endings and tanwīn confirms it is a true noun, not a particle.
3.root: غ-ي-ر (gh-y-r) — to be other, different; otherness, change

4.meaning: A noun meaning 'those who associate partners (with Allah) / polytheists' — the active participle (plural) for people who commit shirk, ascribing partners or equals to Allah. It names them by that defining act.
4.grammar: An active participle (form IV) in the masculine sound plural, with the -īna ending. The mu- prefix forms the doer ('one who associates partners'). The -īna ending is the masculine plural used in the accusative or genitive — i.e. when the word is an object or follows a preposition — as opposed to the -ūna form used for the subject.
4.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — to share, partner; to ascribe partners (to Allah)

5.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
5.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

6.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
6.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

7.meaning: An active verb: 'he associates a partner (with Allah),' i.e. he commits shirk by setting up someone or something as an equal or rival to Allah. The doer here is the one ascribing the partner.
7.grammar: A present-tense active verb. The yu- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'). The final consonant carries a silent/sukūn ending (-ik with no vowel), the jussive form that appears after conditional or negating particles (e.g. 'if he …', 'let him not …').
7.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — to share, to associate as a partner

8.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
8.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
8.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)
