9.meaning: A compound particle meaning 'then it is as though / so it is just as if' — it links to what comes before ('then/so') and introduces a comparison or likeness ('as if, as though') drawing the listener to weigh one thing as equivalent to another.
9.grammar: A cluster of particles, not an inflected word, so it has no case ending. fa- means 'then/so' (linking to a preceding statement); ka- means 'like/as'; anna means 'that (indeed)'; and the attached mā neutralizes anna's normal grammar so the whole reads as the comparison 'as though / just as if.'

10.meaning: 'He/it fell down, came crashing down' — to drop or collapse downward, often with the sound of falling.
10.grammar: A past-tense verb that is third-person masculine singular ('he/it did'). This form takes no person-marking suffix — the bare stem itself means 'he/it', and the -a is just the short vowel (fatḥa) on the stem's final letter, not a separate ending. The doubled final letter reflects the root's two identical last consonants merging into one stressed sound.
10.root: خ-ر-ر (kh-r-r) — to fall/tumble down, to collapse (sometimes with a rushing sound)

11.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
11.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

12.meaning: The sky or heaven — the canopy overhead; the expanse above the earth, also that which is elevated or raised over something. With the definite article it means 'the sky / the heaven'.
12.grammar: A noun with the definite article al- ('the'), in the genitive marked by the -i ending. (The 'l' of al- assimilates in sound into the following 's', a 'sun letter', though it is still written.) The genitive -i ending typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …').

13.meaning: 'Then (she/it) snatches him away' — seizing something suddenly and carrying it off in one swift swoop, the way a bird of prey grabs its catch.
13.grammar: A present-tense verb. fa- means 'then/so'. The ta- prefix marks a feminine-singular subject ('she/it' — in Arabic many plurals of things count as feminine singular). The -u vowel marks the ordinary present tense ('does/is doing'), and the attached -hu means 'him', the one acted upon.
13.root: خ-ط-ف (kh-ṭ-f) — to snatch, seize in a flash

14.meaning: 'The birds' — flying creatures; a collective noun for birds taken as a group.
14.grammar: A definite collective noun. The l- prefix means 'the'. The final -u ending is the nominative case, typically marking the subject — the one doing the action of the verb.

15.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
15.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

16.meaning: '(She/it) plunges / sweeps down' — of wind or a falling thing: to hurl downward from a height, to carry off into a plunge. The same root gives hawā, 'desire', pictured as the soul falling toward what it craves.
16.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ta- prefix marks a feminine-singular subject ('she/it'). The final -ī is not an added ending but part of the verb itself — this root ends in a weak letter, and the long ī is how the ordinary present tense of such verbs sounds ('it plunges').

17.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
17.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

18.meaning: The wind; moving air, a current of air. A common noun for the wind, with the definite article 'the.'
18.grammar: A singular (grammatically feminine) noun meaning 'wind,' made definite by the prefixed al- ('the'). The l of al- assimilates into the following r (so it is pronounced ar-rīḥ). The -u ending marks the nominative case — the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or a thing simply being named.

19.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
19.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

20.meaning: A place, location, spot — the position or site where something is situated. The root relates to being established or located somewhere.
20.grammar: A noun (of place) with the ending -in: the -i is genitive (the case used after a preposition or to link to a preceding noun, '… of/from a place'), and the final -n (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a place').
20.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, come to be

21.meaning: Far-off, remote, out of reach — from a root meaning to crush or grind to dust, so the word evokes a distance so extreme that whatever falls there is pulverized and lost.
21.grammar: An adjective. The -in ending combines two signals: the -i- is the genitive case, which typically shows the word follows a preposition or describes a noun in that case; the final -n (nunation) marks it as indefinite — 'a far-off …' rather than 'the far-off …'.
21.root: س-ح-ق (s-ḥ-q) — to be far; to crush to powder

1.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
1.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

2.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
2.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

3.meaning: He honours, magnifies, holds in reverence — treats something as ʿaẓīm, great, giving it the weight and veneration it deserves.
3.grammar: Present-tense verb: the yu- prefix means 'he'. The doubled middle letter is the intensive pattern (Form II): 'to make great, treat as great'. The bare ending with no final vowel (sukūn) is the shortened jussive mood — the form a verb takes inside an 'if/whoever…' conditional sentence or after a command particle.

4.meaning: 'rites / symbols / sacred emblems' — the distinctive observances and waymarks of devotion (the plural of shaʿīra). They are the visible signs and ceremonies through which reverence is expressed.
4.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural. The final -a ending is accusative. Because this is a 'diptote' plural pattern, it takes a plain -a without the usual 'n' sound; the accusative typically marks a noun as the direct object of a verb.
4.root: ش-ع-ر (sh-ʿ-r) — to be aware, to perceive; hence a token/sign that one is made aware of

5.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
5.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

6.meaning: 'Then indeed it / so truly it (feminine)'. A cluster combining 'so/then', the emphasis particle inna ('truly, indeed'), and 'it' referring to a feminine noun — together stressing strongly that the thing in question really is so.
6.grammar: An emphasis particle inna ('indeed/truly') with fa- ('so/then') in front and the attached pronoun -hā ('it', feminine) as its subject. inna strengthens and affirms the statement that follows; -hā points back to a previously mentioned feminine thing.

7.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
7.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

8.meaning: Taqwā: the vigilant, reverent mindfulness of Allah — literally 'shielding oneself', guarding the soul against His displeasure by staying conscious of Him. Often rendered 'piety' or 'God-fearing', but its core image is protective awareness, not mere emotion.
8.grammar: A verbal noun (a 'doing-word turned thing') built on the pattern ta-…-ā from the root 'to guard'. The final -ā is fixed: nouns ending in this long ā do not change their vowel for case, so the same form serves as subject, object, or after a preposition.

9.meaning: The hearts — plural of qalb, the inner core of a person where understanding, intention, and faith reside. The root means 'to turn over', hinting that the heart is ever-turning and changeable.
9.grammar: A plural noun with the definite article al-. The final -i is the genitive case ending: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the hearts') or shows it follows a preposition.
9.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — to turn, flip over; heart

1.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
1.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

2.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
2.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

3.meaning: Benefits, advantages, useful things — the gains and profitable uses derived from something.
3.grammar: 'Manāfiʿ' is the plural of 'manfaʿa' (benefit), on a diptote plural pattern (mafāʿil). The final '-u' is the nominative ending, generally marking the word as a subject or as what is being described/identified in a sentence.

4.meaning: "to / towards" — a preposition marking the end-point, goal, or direction of a movement or extent ("up to," "as far as," "toward").
4.grammar: An indeclinable preposition; it has no case ending of its own and always governs a following noun in the genitive case.

5.meaning: A noun meaning 'a fixed term, an appointed time, a set deadline, a span allotted before something falls due.' It denotes the limit or end-point of a period.
5.grammar: A noun with the -in ending (with nunation): the genitive indefinite ('a term'). This form occurs after a preposition or in an 'of' linkage with a preceding noun.
5.root: ا-ج-ل (ʾ-j-l) — appointed term, fixed time, deadline

6.meaning: A passive participle meaning 'named, specified, designated, made definite.' It describes something that has been clearly stated and fixed by name — a term that is precisely set rather than vague.
6.grammar: A passive participle (the mu- prefix forms a 'one that is …' word from the Form II intensive pattern, with a doubled middle root letter) meaning 'named/specified.' It carries the indefinite ending -an, written with alif maqṣūra (a final ya-shaped letter sounded as -ā). Because it ends in this weak final letter, the form stays the same whether nominative, accusative, or genitive — context shows it is describing an indefinite noun.
6.root: س-م-ي (s-m-y) — name, naming; to give or assign a name

7.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
7.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

8.meaning: 'Their appointed place/time of falling due' — maḥill is where or when something becomes due and permissible, used especially of the destination where a consecrated sacrificial animal is finally offered.
8.grammar: A noun of place/time from the root 'to alight, become due'. The -u vowel is the nominative case, typically marking the word as the subject or the thing being talked about. The attached -hā means 'their/its' — a feminine pronoun that in Arabic also covers plurals of animals and things.
8.root: ح-ل-ل (ḥ-l-l) — to alight, untie; become due or lawful

9.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
9.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

10.meaning: Al-bayt — the house, dwelling, or home; a place of residence or a building set apart, often used for a household or a place of worship.
10.grammar: A definite noun. The final -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a following noun ('… of …') or follows a preposition or oath particle. The word denotes a house, dwelling, or set-apart sacred building.
10.root: ب-ي-ت (b-y-t) — to spend the night; house, dwelling

11.meaning: The Ancient — ʿatīq means old and venerable, but also noble and set free; as a title of the Kaʿbah it carries both senses: the most ancient sanctuary, and one freed from the grip of tyrants.
11.grammar: An adjective with al- 'the'. Adjectives mirror the case of the noun they describe, so its genitive -i ending matches a preceding genitive noun — the -i is the case that follows prepositions or an 'of'-link.
11.root: ع-ت-ق (ʿ-t-q) — being ancient; being freed; nobility

1.meaning: 'And for every / for each' — assigns or relates something to each individual member of a class, with the sense 'and to every (one) …'.
1.grammar: The quantifier 'kull' ('every/each/all') preceded by 'wa' ('and') and the preposition 'li' ('for/to'). The final '-i' is the genitive case, the form regularly taken after a preposition.

2.meaning: A community, nation, or people — a body of people bound together by shared faith, way of life, or origin; one collective group.
2.grammar: A feminine noun. The final -in (genitive with 'nunation') marks it as indefinite ('a community') and links it to a preceding noun or preposition ('… of a community'). The feminine -t sound surfaces before the ending.

3.meaning: We made, rendered, set up, or appointed. A completed act of making or designating, done by a group or by a majestic 'We.'
3.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb with the attached subject ending -nā, meaning 'we' did the action. 'Jaʿala' carries senses from 'to make/create' to 'to render X into Y' or 'to appoint.'
3.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, render, appoint, place

4.meaning: A rite — an appointed act, place, or occasion of devotion, used especially of ritual sacrifice. From the root of nusuk, wholehearted devotional service to Allah.
4.grammar: A noun. The -an ending combines the accusative case — typically marking the direct object, the thing given or made — with nunation (the final -n), which signals indefiniteness: 'A rite', not 'the rite'. In writing this -an is spelled with the doubled-vowel mark plus a silent supporting alif.

5.meaning: 'So that they may mention/remember' — dhikr covers both remembering in the heart and mentioning on the tongue, so the verb means to invoke and call to mind, especially the name of Allah.
5.grammar: A present-tense verb in the subjunctive mood. li- means 'so that', stating purpose. ya- marks a third-person subject and the -ū ending makes it plural ('they'). After li- the usual final -na of the plural is dropped — that clipped ending is exactly what signals 'in order that they may …' rather than a plain statement.

6.meaning: Name — the word or designation by which someone or something is called; in worship, the invoking of a name (especially Allah's) over an act.
6.grammar: A noun ('ism,' 'name'). The final '-a' (fatḥa) is the accusative case, the form typically used when the word is the direct object of a verb — the thing being acted upon.
6.root: س-م-و (s-m-w) — height, loftiness; the source of 'ism' (name)

7.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
7.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

8.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
8.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

9.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
9.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

10.meaning: He provided them, He gave them sustenance — rizq is provision in the widest sense: food, livelihood, every good thing Allah supplies.
10.grammar: A past-tense verb: the final -a of razaqa marks 'he' (third person masculine singular) in the perfect tense — a completed act of providing. The attached pronoun -hum ('them') is the direct object, so the one word says 'he provided them'.

11.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
11.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

12.meaning: Beast, grazing animal — literally 'the mute one', an animal that cannot speak; used of cattle and livestock.
12.grammar: A feminine noun (the tāʾ marbūṭah ending is pronounced -t when another word follows). The -i ending is the genitive: it typically links the word to a neighbouring noun in an 'of'-relationship or follows a preposition. Having no al- and no nunation, it stands in a construct chain — 'the beast of…'.
12.root: ب-ه-م (b-h-m) — being mute, indistinct; hence dumb animals

13.meaning: 'the grazing livestock / cattle' — a collective term for domesticated herd animals such as camels, cattle, sheep, and goats, valued as wealth and as a provision.
13.grammar: A definite noun ('the …') with the -i (genitive) ending, which typically links it to a preceding noun in a possessive 'of …' relationship or follows a preposition. It is itself a plural of naʿam (livestock).
13.root: ن-ع-م (n-ʿ-m) — softness, ease; grazing livestock, bounty/blessing

14.meaning: 'So your God …' — ilāh is 'a god, an object of worship', anything taken as worthy of devotion; with 'your' it points to the one deity who truly deserves the worship of those addressed.
14.grammar: A noun with pieces on both sides. fa- means 'so/then', drawing a conclusion. The -u vowel is the nominative case, typically marking the subject — the one about whom something is declared. The attached -kum means 'your' addressed to a group ('you all').

15.meaning: A god / an object of worship — a being taken as a deity and worshipped. As an indefinite noun it means 'a god' in the general sense.
15.grammar: A singular noun. The -un ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a god') and in the nominative case, typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate.
15.root: أ-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — godhood, worship, being a deity

16.meaning: One / single and unique — denoting oneness: a single individual, undivided and without partner or plurality.
16.grammar: An adjective/numeral meaning 'one.' The -un ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite and in the nominative case, the case typically used for a subject, predicate, or a descriptor agreeing with such a noun.

17.meaning: So for him / then his is; a linking word 'so/then' joined to 'for him,' expressing that something belongs or accrues to a single male — 'so to him belongs…'
17.grammar: A cluster of particles: the connector fa- ('so, then, and as a result') + the preposition la- ('for, belonging to') + the pronoun -hu ('him'). Together they assign possession or entitlement to a single male: 'so for him (is)…'

18.meaning: 'Submit!' — a plural command to surrender oneself wholly to Allah. Form IV of the root of salām ('peace, wholeness'): to hand oneself over intact, entering into peace through obedience; the verb behind the words islām and muslim.
18.grammar: An imperative (command) verb in Form IV, whose a- opening is part of the command stem itself. The -ū ending marks the command as addressed to a group: 'you all, submit!'.

19.meaning: A two-part word: 'and' + a command 'give glad tidings, bring good news.' The verb means to announce something joyful that shows on the face — to cheer someone with happy news. It is the standard word for delivering good tidings.
19.grammar: A conjunction 'wa' + an imperative (command) verb, addressed to a single male ('you, give good news'). The base form is bashshir; the final -i here is a connecting vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word, not a case ending. The doubled middle letter marks an intensive/causative sense: actively bringing good news to someone.

20.meaning: The humbly devoted ones — mukhbit describes a heart that has settled low and still before its Lord, from a root meaning low, tranquil ground; people of quiet, unresisting humility toward Allah.
20.grammar: An active participle ('one who does…') with the definite article al-. The mu- opening is the participle marker, roughly '-ing person'. The -īna ending is the masculine plural in the accusative/genitive form: it typically appears when the group is the object of an action or follows a preposition.
20.root: خ-ب-ت (kh-b-t) — low, tranquil ground; to be humble

1.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
1.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

2.meaning: 'When' — a particle introducing a time or circumstance, generally pointing to something expected or definite to come ('when/whenever it happens'). It sets up a condition or moment whose outcome then follows.
2.grammar: An indeclinable adverb/particle of time; it has no case ending and never changes form. It typically introduces a clause about a future or recurring event ('when …'), and is normally followed by a verb describing what takes place.

3.meaning: It was mentioned, named, invoked, or called to remembrance; the passive sense of bringing something to speech or recall.
3.grammar: A past-tense passive verb (Form I), third-person masculine singular ('it was …'). The internal vowel pattern — u after the first radical, i after the second (dhukir-) — is the diagnostic of the Form I passive, with no agent named. The final -a is the third-person masculine singular past ending. A triliteral Form I has no internal affix, so the stem is not further divisible.
3.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — remembrance, mention, calling to mind

4.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
4.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

5.meaning: They (feminine) became fearful, were stirred with awe, or trembled. Describes hearts being gripped by reverential fear and a quaking sense of dread before something tremendous.
5.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -at ending marks a third-person feminine singular subject ('she/it did'), commonly used when the doer is a grammatically feminine noun such as 'hearts'.
5.root: و-ج-ل (w-j-l) — fear mixed with awe; an inward trembling and dread.

6.meaning: 'Their hearts' — the hearts belonging to a masculine plural group. In Qur'anic usage the 'heart' is the seat of understanding, intention, feeling, and faith, not merely the physical organ.
6.grammar: A plural noun ('hearts') in the nominative, shown by the -u before the pronoun, which typically marks it as the subject of a sentence. The attached 'hum' means 'their' (a group of males or mixed group), giving 'their hearts.'
6.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — heart; to turn over, fluctuate

7.meaning: 'And those who are patient / the steadfast' — people who endure hardship with calm, self-restrained perseverance, holding firm without complaint. Joined by 'and'.
7.grammar: The connector wa ('and'), the definite article (its 'l' assimilated into the following sun letter 'ṣ'), the active participle 'one who is patient', and the sound masculine plural ending -īna. The active participle names the doer of the quality; the -īna ending marks the masculine plural in the genitive or accusative case.

8.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
8.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

9.meaning: A word meaning 'what' or 'that which' — a relative/indefinite particle pointing to an unspecified thing ('what', 'whatever', 'that which').
9.grammar: An invariable particle (mā) with no case ending. Depending on context it works as a relative pronoun ('that which') introducing a clause, or as an interrogative/indefinite ('what'). It does not inflect for case, gender, or number.

10.meaning: It struck or befell them — said of something (typically an affliction, hardship, or event) that reached and afflicted a group of people. The verb conveys hitting a target or something landing upon someone.
10.grammar: A past-tense verb (he/it did) in the third-person masculine singular, here in its causative 'af'ala' pattern (to make something hit/reach). The attached -hum is an object pronoun meaning 'them', so the whole reads 'it befell them'.
10.root: ص-و-ب (ṣ-w-b) — to hit the mark, to be correct/apt; (of rain or affliction) to come down upon

11.meaning: 'And the ones who establish / keep up …' — muqīm is the active participle of aqāma, 'to make stand, maintain properly and constantly'; used of those who perform a duty fully and keep it standing, not merely do it once.

parts.en: plural ending (shortened before a following noun)

11.grammar: wa- means 'and'; al- is 'the'. The mu- opening marks an active participle ('one who …-s'). The -ī ending is the masculine plural with its usual final -na dropped: that clipping happens when the word is bound tightly to a noun right after it, meaning 'the establishers OF …'.
11.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand; make upright, maintain

12.meaning: 'The prayer' — al-ṣalāh, the formal act of worship and supplication; the ritual standing, bowing, and prostrating before Allah that is a pillar of the faith.
12.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending (on the tā' marbūṭa) is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding preposition or oath particle, or to a following noun in a possessive '… of …' relationship.

13.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and from/out of that which' or 'and from what'. It joins a new item to what precedes and points to an unspecified thing or category ('whatever it is that...').
13.grammar: A combination of the connector wa ('and'), the preposition min ('from, out of, part of'), and the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). The nūn of min has assimilated into the mīm of mā, doubling it (mim-mā). The whole phrase is invariable and does not take case endings.

14.meaning: 'We provided/bestowed upon them': the act of granting sustenance and provision — food, wealth, and every good thing a creature lives on — given to a group of people. The verb conveys provision freely supplied by a giver.
14.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -nā suffix is the subject 'we' (a past-tense form meaning the action is completed). The attached -hum is the object pronoun 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group). So the structure is 'we + [verb] + them'.
14.root: ر-ز-ق (r-z-q) — to provide, to grant sustenance/provision

15.meaning: 'They spend/give out': to expend wealth or provision, especially by giving it away in charity and in good causes. The word centers on disbursing what one has rather than hoarding it.
15.grammar: A present/future-tense verb in Form IV (anfaqa, 'to spend, expend'). The imperfect prefix is only yu-; the nūn that follows is the first root letter (of ن-ف-ق), not part of the prefix. The yu- prefix together with the -ūna ending marks the subject as 'they' (masculine plural) doing the action now or habitually. The -ūna ending also signals the indicative mood, the default 'plain' form used for ongoing or repeated action.
15.root: ن-ف-ق (n-f-q) — to spend, expend, give out

1.meaning: 'And the budn' — plural of badanah: the large-bodied sacrificial animals, especially camels (and by extension cattle), set apart for offering. Named from badan, 'body', for their bulk.
1.grammar: wa- means 'and'; al- is 'the'. The final -a is the accusative case ending: it typically marks the word as the object — the thing acted upon, appointed, or made.

2.meaning: We made it / We appointed it / We rendered it — to bring something about, set it in a state, or assign it a purpose. The verb can mean 'to make,' 'to place,' or 'to turn (something) into.'
2.grammar: A past-tense verb. The suffix -nā marks the doer as 'we', and the attached -hā ('it/her') is the object receiving the action — so the whole means 'we made it'. The combination conveys a completed act done by a group (or the majestic 'We').
2.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, place, set, appoint, render into

3.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
3.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

4.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
4.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

5.meaning: The rites/emblems — shaʿāʾir is the plural of shaʿīrah: a marked-out sign of devotion, an outward observance appointed as a visible token of worship. From the root 'to perceive, mark', so a shaʿīrah is something set up to be noticed and honored.
5.grammar: A plural noun. The final -i is the genitive case ending: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the rites') or to a following possessor, or shows it comes after a preposition.
5.root: ش-ع-ر (sh-ʿ-r) — to perceive, be aware; a mark

6.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
6.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

7.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
7.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

8.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
8.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

9.meaning: 'Better / best; good' — an adjective of comparison meaning more good, preferable, or superior. It also serves broadly for 'goodness' and that which is good and beneficial.
9.grammar: A noun/adjective bearing the ending -un (nunation): the doubled-u 'n' sound marks the word as both indefinite ('a/an', no 'the') and nominative — the case used for the subject of a sentence or the predicate that describes it.
9.root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r) — good, goodness, that which is choice and beneficial

10.meaning: A call to remember, mention, invoke, or call to mind — especially to remember Allah by mentioning Him and being mindful of Him. The opening 'then/so' links the command to something preceding.

parts.en: remember / mention! (command stem with plural wāw)

10.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a group: the -ū ending means 'you (plural masculine), do it!'. The prefixed fa- means 'then' or 'so', connecting the order to a preceding statement or condition. The initial alif is a helping vowel to make the command pronounceable.
10.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, mention, call to mind, invoke

11.meaning: Name — the word or designation by which someone or something is called; in worship, the invoking of a name (especially Allah's) over an act.
11.grammar: A noun ('ism,' 'name'). The final '-a' (fatḥa) is the accusative case, the form typically used when the word is the direct object of a verb — the thing being acted upon.
11.root: س-م-و (s-m-w) — height, loftiness; the source of 'ism' (name)

12.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
12.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

13.meaning: 'On it / upon it / over it' — the preposition 'alā ('on, upon, against') joined to the pronoun 'it/her', referring to a single feminine or grammatically feminine thing.
13.grammar: 'ʿalā' is a preposition meaning 'on/upon/over'; its ending shifts to -ay when a pronoun is attached. The suffix -hā is the object pronoun for a single feminine (or feminine-gender) thing. Together they mean 'on it'. Words after a preposition stand in the genitive, though attached pronouns like -hā do not visibly change form.

14.meaning: 'Standing in rows / lined up' — plural describing animals drawn up side by side in orderly ranks, as camels are stood in line for sacrifice.
14.grammar: A plural adjective-noun of a pattern that takes only a single case vowel (a 'diptote') and no indefinite -n. The final -a is the accusative; on a word like this it typically marks a state or condition — describing HOW the subject is while something is done ('… while lined up').
14.root: ص-ف-ف (ṣ-f-f) — to set in a row, line up

15.meaning: A connecting phrase meaning 'then when / and when', introducing a circumstance whose occurrence triggers a following response. 'Fa-' links it to what precedes; 'idhā' sets up a 'when … (then) …' condition for something expected to happen.
15.grammar: A particle cluster, not a noun or verb, so it has no case ending. 'Idhā' is a conditional/temporal particle ('when') used for events regarded as bound to occur, and it normally introduces a clause followed by a main response. The prefixed fa- ('then/so') ties the whole condition to the preceding statement.
15.root: — (particles)

16.meaning: '(She/it) fell / came down' — wajaba means to fall with a thud and, from that, 'to become due, obligatory' (the same root gives wājib, a binding duty): when a thing falls, it lands and is settled.
16.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -at ending marks a completed action by a feminine-singular subject ('she/it fell') — and in Arabic plurals of animals and things routinely take this feminine-singular form.
16.root: و-ج-ب (w-j-b) — to fall, land; be obligatory

17.meaning: 'Their sides/flanks' — junūb is the plural of janb, the side of the body; of an animal, the flank on which it comes to rest when it falls.
17.grammar: A plural noun. The -u vowel is the nominative case, typically marking the subject — the thing that does or undergoes the falling, standing, etc. The attached -hā is the feminine pronoun 'their/its', which Arabic uses for plurals of animals and things.

18.meaning: 'Then eat!' — a command to a group to eat, joined by 'then / so', which links it as a following or resulting step.
18.grammar: An imperative (command) verb prefixed with fa- 'then/so', which marks sequence or consequence ('and then…', 'so…'). The -ū ending aims the command at a group ('you all, eat!'). This verb drops its original first root letter, so the stem is just kul-. The silent alif after the wāw spells the plural ending.

19.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'min' ('from / out of / some of') joined to the pronoun 'it' (feminine). Together: 'from it / out of it / of it,' indicating a source or a portion taken from a feminine thing.
19.grammar: A preposition 'min' with the attached pronoun '-hā' ('it/her'), referring to a feminine noun. 'Min' indicates origin, source, or a part taken from a whole; the attached pronoun is in the object form required after a preposition.

20.meaning: And feed — give food to, cause someone to eat. A command of generosity: put food into the hands of another.
20.grammar: A plural command: the a- prefix with this verb pattern (Form IV, the causative) turns 'eat' into 'make eat, feed', and the -ū ending addresses a group — 'you all, feed!'. Wa- joins it to a preceding command.
20.root: ط-ع-م (ṭ-ʿ-m) — food, tasting, eating

21.meaning: The contented poor — qāniʿ is one who is satisfied with what he has (or with what he is given) and does not beg; classically, the needy person who holds back from asking.

parts.en: contented one, who does not beg (active participle)

21.grammar: An active participle ('one who is …-ing/-ed') with the definite article al-. The final -a is the accusative case ending: it typically marks the word as the object — the one to whom something is given or done.

22.meaning: 'And the one who presents himself' — muʿtarr is the needy person who comes near and shows himself hoping to be given, whether or not he asks aloud; the seeker who approaches.

parts.en: one who presents himself seeking (active participle)

22.grammar: wa- means 'and'; al- is 'the'. The mu- opening marks an active participle of a derived verb form ('one who …-s'). The final -a is the accusative case ending, typically marking the word as an object — one to whom something is given.
22.root: ع-ر-ر (ʿ-r-r) — to approach, present oneself (seeking a favor)

23.meaning: 'Like that / thus / in this manner.' A comparison word meaning that something is done or is the case in the way just mentioned.
23.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like/as') prefixed to the demonstrative 'that'. Together they form a fixed adverbial expression, 'like that / thus', which does not change its ending with grammatical position.
23.root: — (a particle of comparison joined to a demonstrative; no root)

24.meaning: We made them subservient — brought them under control and placed them at someone's service. The verb sakhkhara means to tame or harness something so it serves a purpose, as Allah subjects creatures and forces of nature for human benefit.
24.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in the intensive Form II pattern, which implies thoroughly subjecting something. The -nā suffix marks the subject 'we' (the royal 'We' when Allah speaks); the final -hā is an attached object pronoun 'them/it' — Arabic uses this feminine singular pronoun for plurals of non-human things.

25.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
25.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

26.meaning: 'so that you may…,' 'in the hope that you…' — a particle expressing purpose, expectation, or hopeful anticipation, fused with 'you (plural).' It introduces a hoped-for or intended outcome; when used of Allah it conveys the desired result rather than uncertainty.

parts.en: so that / perhaps / in hope that

26.grammar: An emphatic particle of hope/purpose belonging to the 'inna' family, which attaches a pronoun as its subject. The particle's fixed form ends in '-a,' and the suffix '-kum' is 'you (plural),' giving 'so that you (all) may…'

27.meaning: 'You (all) give thanks / are grateful'. To recognize a kindness and acknowledge it — with the heart, tongue, and deeds — toward the one who bestowed it.
27.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb. The 'ta-' prefix signals a 'you' subject, and the '-ūna' ending marks a plural masculine 'you' in the ongoing (indicative) mood — 'you all give thanks'. The retained '-na' shows the verb stands free of any negating or governing particle.

1.meaning: 'Never / will not' — a particle that negates a future action emphatically. Lan denies that something will ever happen, stronger and more absolute than a simple 'not'.
1.grammar: A negating particle that applies to present-tense verbs to deny them in the future ('will never…'). Grammatically it also puts the following verb into the subjunctive mood, which clips that verb's ending to a short -a. Lan itself does not change.

2.meaning: That (he/it) may reach or attain — to get through to something and actually obtain it. Used of something arriving at, touching, or attaining its goal.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb; the ya- prefix means 'he/it'. The final -a is the subjunctive mood ending, which appears after particles like 'an (that), lan (never will), or li- (so that) — it typically turns the verb into 'that it may…' or 'will never…' rather than a plain statement.

3.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
3.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

4.meaning: Their flesh / their meats — luḥūm is the plural of laḥm, the flesh or meat of an animal.
4.grammar: A plural noun. The -u ending is the nominative case, marking the word as the subject or doer in a sentence. The attached -hā means 'their' — the feminine singular pronoun Arabic uses to refer back to plurals of non-human things (such as animals).

5.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
5.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

6.meaning: Their blood — dimā' is the plural of dam, blood; the plural covers the blood of many animals.
6.grammar: A plural noun. The -u ending is the nominative case, marking the subject of a sentence; because the word ends in hamza followed by this u-vowel, the hamza is written seated on a wāw (ؤ). The attached -hā means 'their', referring back to non-human plurals with a feminine singular pronoun, as Arabic regularly does.

7.meaning: 'But / however / yet' — a particle of correction and contrast that sets aside what came before and affirms something different instead.
7.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to lākin ('but / however'). Lākin is a particle of rectification: it draws a contrast with, or corrects, the preceding idea and introduces an opposing or qualifying statement ('... but rather...').

8.meaning: Reaches him / attains him — the verb of reaching and obtaining with an attached pronoun object: something arrives at or gets through to him.
8.grammar: A present-tense verb; ya- means 'he/it'. The -u before the pronoun is the indicative mood ending, marking a plain factual statement ('it does reach'). The final -hu is the attached object pronoun 'him'.

9.meaning: Taqwā — a key Qur'anic concept: a deep consciousness of Allah and reverent mindfulness that moves one to guard against wrongdoing and shield oneself from Allah's displeasure; often rendered 'piety, mindful fear of Allah, righteousness'. Joined to the definite article 'the'.
9.grammar: The l- prefix is the definite article 'the' (its 'l' assimilates to the following 't', written with a shadda). The word ends in a fixed long -ā (alif maqṣūra) that does not change for case; such words show no visible case ending, so the form is the same whether subject, object, or possessor.

10.meaning: A combination meaning 'from among you' or 'of you' — singling out a part or some individuals out of a larger group being addressed.
10.grammar: The preposition min ('from, among, some of') with the attached pronoun -kum, which means 'you' for a group of two or more (grammatically masculine plural). Because the pronoun follows a preposition, it is in the object form; the whole expression partitions or draws out individuals from the addressed group.
10.root: — (min is a particle/preposition; -kum is a pronoun)

11.meaning: 'Like that / thus / in this manner.' A comparison word meaning that something is done or is the case in the way just mentioned.
11.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like/as') prefixed to the demonstrative 'that'. Together they form a fixed adverbial expression, 'like that / thus', which does not change its ending with grammatical position.
11.root: — (a particle of comparison joined to a demonstrative; no root)

12.meaning: He subjected it / He put it in service — to bring something under control and compel it to work at one's command; the word connotes subjugating a powerful force that would otherwise be unmanageable.

parts.en: it / her (third person feminine singular object pronoun)

12.grammar: Form II perfect (past) tense verb, third person masculine singular, with a third-person feminine singular object pronoun -ha attached. The Form II pattern (fa'ala) often carries a causative or intensive sense — here: to completely subject and subordinate. The -ha suffix refers back to a feminine noun (such as the wind).
12.root: س-خ-ر (s-kh-r) — to subject, press into service, subdue

13.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
13.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

14.meaning: So that you (all) may magnify — declare the greatness of. The Form II verb kabbara means to proclaim someone supremely great, as in saying 'Allāhu akbar' (takbīr).
14.grammar: The li- prefix means 'so that / in order to' and puts the verb in the subjunctive: with plural 'you' verbs the subjunctive shows itself by dropping the usual final -na, leaving just -ū. The tu- prefix marks 'you', and -ū marks the plural — together 'so that you all may…'. The verb is the intensive Form II pattern: actively declaring greatness, not merely thinking it.

15.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
15.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.
15.root: — (proper name)

16.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
16.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

17.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
17.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

18.meaning: A verb meaning 'He guided you (plural)' — to show the right way, lead aright, or direct toward what is correct, with 'you all' as the ones guided.
18.grammar: A past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he guided'), built on a weak root so its final letter appears as a long -ā (written with a dagger alif). The attached -kum is the plural object pronoun, 'you all', i.e. the people guided.

19.meaning: A two-part word: 'and' + a command 'give glad tidings, bring good news.' The verb means to announce something joyful that shows on the face — to cheer someone with happy news. It is the standard word for delivering good tidings.
19.grammar: A conjunction 'wa' + an imperative (command) verb, addressed to a single male ('you, give good news'). The base form is bashshir; the final -i here is a connecting vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word, not a case ending. The doubled middle letter marks an intensive/causative sense: actively bringing good news to someone.

20.meaning: 'The doers of good / those who act with excellence and beauty'. It denotes people who do what is good and do it well — acting righteously, generously, and with sincerity, as if conscious of being watched by Allah.

parts.en: good-doers / those who excel in doing good

20.grammar: A definite plural active participle (the 'doer' form of the verb 'to do good'). The prefixed al- means 'the'. The ending -īna marks a sound masculine plural in the object/oblique state — the form used when the noun is a direct object or follows a preposition. It refers to male (or mixed) persons characterized by the action.
20.root: ح-س-ن (ḥ-s-n) — to be good, beautiful; to do well and excellently

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
2.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

3.meaning: Defends / wards off on behalf of — the Form III verb dāfaʿa pictures ongoing, engaged repelling: pushing away whatever attacks, championing and protecting someone.
3.grammar: A present-tense verb in Form III, a pattern that often implies directed, sustained engagement — here, actively repelling on someone's behalf. The yu- prefix means 'he'; the final -u is the indicative mood, the ending of a plain factual statement, and the present tense suggests continuous, ongoing defence.

4.meaning: About / concerning; a particle marking the topic of inquiry or the thing one moves away from.
4.grammar: A preposition meaning 'about, concerning, away from'. Its base form is ʿan; the final -i here is a helping vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a connecting 'al-'. It governs the genitive case on whatever noun follows.

5.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
5.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

6.meaning: They believed, they came to faith; to place trust and security in something and affirm it as true (the inner act of faith).
6.grammar: A past-tense verb of the Form IV (causative) pattern. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they') for a completed action ('they believed'). The final written alif after the wāw is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

7.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
7.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

8.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
8.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

9.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
9.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

10.meaning: He loves / likes / holds dear. To have affection for and approval of something or someone.
10.grammar: A present-tense verb in the fourth pattern, third-person masculine singular ('he…'). The yu- prefix signals a single masculine subject, and the final -u ending marks the indicative mood, presenting the action as an established fact or ongoing reality.
10.root: ح-ب-ب (ḥ-b-b) — love, affection; to hold dear

11.meaning: All, every, the whole of — totality. When followed by a singular it means 'every (one)'; when followed by a definite plural or whole it means 'all of.'
11.grammar: A noun of totality, almost always joined to a following noun in the genitive ('every … / all of …'). The final -a is the accusative case, the form used when the word functions as an object of a verb.

12.meaning: Utterly treacherous — an intensive adjective from khāna (to betray). The doubled-middle pattern khawwān describes a habitual, repeated betrayer of trust, not someone who slipped once.
12.grammar: An intensive adjective pattern (faʿʿāl) that turns 'one who betrays' into 'one given to constant betrayal'. The -in ending is the genitive case with nunation (tanwīn): the genitive typically follows a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('of…'), and the tanwīn marks it as indefinite — 'a/any treacherous one'.

13.meaning: Deeply ungrateful — an intensive adjective from kafara, which spans both ingratitude and disbelief (literally 'covering over' a favour or the truth). Kafūr is one who persistently refuses to acknowledge blessings.
13.grammar: An intensive adjective pattern (faʿūl) meaning given over to ingratitude as a settled trait. The -in ending is the genitive case with nunation: the genitive usually follows a preposition or a possessing noun, and the tanwīn signals indefiniteness — 'a/any ingrate'.

1.meaning: Permission has been given — the passive of adhina (to permit, to grant leave). The doer is left unnamed by the grammar itself; the focus falls entirely on the fact that leave is now granted.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb in the passive voice: the internal vowel pattern u-i (udhina rather than adhina) is what marks the passive in Arabic — 'it was permitted' with no doer stated. The final -a is the normal ending of a 3rd-person masculine singular past verb.
1.root: أ-ذ-ن (ʾ-dh-n) — permitting, giving leave (related to the ear/listening)

2.meaning: A compound meaning 'for those who' or 'belonging to those who'. It joins the preposition 'for/to' with a masculine plural relative pronoun ('those who'), introducing a clause that describes a group of people by something they do or possess.
2.grammar: The prefix 'li-' is a preposition meaning 'for', 'to', or expressing ownership/benefit ('belonging to'). The relative pronoun is 'alladhīna' ('those who'), but when 'li-' attaches to it the connecting hamza of 'al-' drops out and the two lām sounds merge into one doubled lām, so the form is written and read 'lilladhīna' rather than 'li-alladhīna'. 'alladhīna' has a fixed shape and does not change for case.

3.meaning: They are being fought — the passive of the Form III verb qātala (to fight someone, to do battle): they are on the receiving end of warfare, attacked rather than attacking.
3.grammar: A present-tense passive verb: the yu- prefix with the internal ā-a vowelling marks the passive of Form III — 'they are fought against' rather than 'they fight'. The -ūna ending marks a masculine plural subject in the indicative mood, the form of a plain ongoing statement.

4.meaning: A connector meaning 'because they…' or 'by reason that they…'. It fuses the preposition bi- (here giving a cause, 'because of') with anna ('that', an emphatic particle introducing a fact) and the attached pronoun -hum ('they').
4.grammar: bi- here gives a causal sense ('because of'). anna is an emphatic particle meaning 'that' which introduces a statement of fact and takes a following noun or pronoun in the accusative; the attached -hum is that pronoun, a masculine plural 'they'. Together they give a reason: 'because they …'.

5.meaning: A third-person plural past-tense passive verb meaning 'they were wronged / treated unjustly / oppressed.' It marks people as the recipients of injustice done to them.
5.grammar: Past-tense passive verb (the internal vowel pattern u-i signals 'the action was done to them, not by them'). The '-ū' ending marks the subject as 'they' (masculine plural), here the ones to whom the wrong was done.
5.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — wrongdoing, injustice, oppression, putting something out of its rightful place

6.meaning: 'And indeed' / 'and truly' — the joining word 'wa' ('and') attached to the emphatic particle 'inna', which introduces a statement and strongly affirms it, adding certainty like 'surely' or 'indeed'.
6.grammar: A connective 'wa' ('and') plus 'inna', a particle of emphasis that opens a nominal sentence. 'Inna' puts its following noun (the subject) into the accusative case while strongly affirming the truth of the statement.

7.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
7.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

8.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
8.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

9.meaning: Their help / their victory — naṣr is aid that carries someone through to triumph; with the pronoun, the helping-to-victory of them.
9.grammar: A verbal noun ('helping / giving victory'). The -i ending is the genitive case, which typically follows a preposition or ties the word to a preceding noun ('…of…'). The attached -him means 'their / them' (masculine plural); with a verbal noun it can name either the helpers or, commonly, the ones being helped.

10.meaning: Surely All-Able — qadīr is the intensive adjective of power: fully, permanently capable of whatever is measured out, one of the names describing Allah. The la- prefix adds emphatic force: 'most certainly'.
10.grammar: The la- prefix is an emphatic particle, often paired with 'inna' constructions, stressing certainty: 'surely'. Qadīr is an intensive adjective pattern (faʿīl) meaning possessing power as an enduring attribute. The -un ending is the nominative case with nunation, the case used for a subject or a predicate ('X *is* surely able').

1.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
1.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

2.meaning: They were expelled, they were driven out — the passive past-tense verb; refers to being forced to leave one's home.
2.grammar: A passive past-tense verb (Form IV passive), third person masculine plural. The -ū suffix marks masculine plural subject. The passive is formed by changing the vowel pattern: active akhraja → passive ukhrija. The -ū shortens before the final vowel in passive plural.
2.root: خ-ر-ج (kh-r-j) — to go out, exit; Form IV akhraja means to expel/drive out; the passive ukhrija means 'they were expelled'

3.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
3.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

4.meaning: 'Their dwellings / homes / abodes' — the houses and homelands where people live.
4.grammar: A plural noun (singular dār, 'dwelling') with the attached pronoun -him ('their'). The -i vowel before the pronoun is the genitive case, which typically follows a preposition or links the noun in a possessive 'of' relationship; here the possession is expressed by the attached 'their.'
4.root: د-و-ر (d-w-r) — turning, encircling; a dwelling as an enclosed/encircled place

5.meaning: 'Without' or 'other than' — the preposition bi- joined to ghayr, a noun meaning 'other than / not / lacking', together conveying the absence of something ('with no …', 'wrongfully').
5.grammar: bi- is a preposition that takes the genitive; ghayr is a noun of exception/negation ('other than'). Its -i ending is genitive (required after bi-) and it also links to a following noun in a possessive 'of' relationship, so 'bi-ghayri X' means 'without X / other than X'.
5.root: غ-ي-ر (gh-y-r) — otherness, difference, being other than

6.meaning: Right / just cause / truth — ḥaqq is what is true, valid, and due: a rightful claim, justice, reality as opposed to falsehood. A weighty word covering both 'truth' and 'legitimate right'.
6.grammar: A noun. The -in ending is the genitive case with nunation (tanwīn): the genitive typically follows a preposition or completes a phrase like 'without any…', and the tanwīn marks indefiniteness — 'a/any right'.

7.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
7.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

8.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
8.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

9.meaning: Verb meaning 'they say / they would say' — the act of speaking or uttering words, attributed to a masculine plural group.
9.grammar: A present-tense verb, masculine third-person plural ('they'). The dropped final 'nūn' (yaqūlū rather than yaqūlūna) shows it is in the subjunctive or jussive mood — the form used after particles meaning 'so that,' 'in order to,' or in conditional answers, rather than as a plain statement.

10.meaning: 'Our Lord' — 'Rabb' (Lord, Master, Sustainer who creates, owns, nurtures and governs) joined to 'our'. A weighty term for Allah as the One who brings up and sustains all that exists.
10.grammar: A noun with the attached possessive pronoun '-nā' ('our'). The -u before the pronoun is the nominative case, used when the word is the subject or predicate of a sentence ('[He] is our Lord').
10.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master; lordship

11.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
11.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

12.meaning: "and were it not for / and if not for" — a compound particle introducing a hypothetical: it points to something whose existence prevents a stated consequence, i.e. 'had it not been for X, then Y would have happened'.

parts.en: were it not for / if not

12.grammar: A particle phrase, not a verb, so it carries no case or tense ending. It sets up a conditional that is contrary to fact, typically answered by a clause beginning with la- ('then certainly…'). The leading wa- is the connector 'and'.

13.meaning: "repelling / pushing back / warding off" — a verbal noun naming the act of driving something away or holding it back, the abstract idea of repulsion or defence.
13.grammar: A verbal noun (the action named as a thing). The final -u ending is the nominative case, the form a noun takes as a subject or as the leading term in a possessive chain ('the repelling OF …').
13.root: د-ف-ع (d-f-ʿ) — to push, repel, ward off

14.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
14.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

15.meaning: Mankind, humanity, people in general — the collective of human beings.
15.grammar: A definite noun ('the people') with the attached 'al-' ('the'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (a sun letter), which is why the 'n' is doubled — this is a pronunciation effect, not a separate piece. The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the one being acted upon) or the subject of certain particles.
15.root: ن-و-س (n-w-s) — to move/sway; by extension, people

16.meaning: "some of them / a part of them" — the word baʿḍ means 'a portion/some', and with the attached pronoun it means 'some of them', singling out part of a group.
16.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive/partitive pronoun. The -a ending is the accusative case, the form a noun takes as the object of an action or the second term of certain constructions. The suffix -hum means 'them' (third-person masculine plural).

17.meaning: 'In part / in some' — referring to a portion or some of a whole, here left indefinite. The bi- prefix gives the sense of disbelieving 'in' something.
17.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with') plus the noun baʿḍ ('a part, some'). The final -in (tanwīn kasr) is the genitive case with indefiniteness, required after bi- and marking the noun as 'some (unspecified) part.'
17.root: ب-ع-ض (b-ʿ-ḍ) — a part, portion, or some of a whole

18.meaning: Would surely have been demolished — the passive of the intensive Form II haddama, to tear down completely, raze to the ground. The la- prefix adds strong emphasis: 'certainly would have been'.
18.grammar: A past-tense passive verb: the u-i vowelling (huddima) marks the passive — 'was torn down' with no doer named — and the doubled middle letter (Form II) intensifies it: utterly razed. The la- prefix is the emphatic particle that typically answers a 'had it not been / if' clause: 'then surely…'. The final -t marks a feminine (here, plural non-human) subject.

19.meaning: Monasteries / monks' cells — ṣawāmiʿ is the plural of ṣawmaʿa, the secluded cell or cloister of a Christian monk; by extension, monasteries as places of Christian devotion.
19.grammar: A broken (internal-change) plural. The -u ending is the nominative case, marking a subject. Notice there is no tanwīn (-un): this plural pattern belongs to the 'diptote' class of nouns, which never take nunation.
19.root: ص-م-ع (ṣ-m-ʿ) — tapering, seclusion (whence the monk's cell)

20.meaning: And churches — biyaʿ is the plural of bīʿa, a Christian church or place of worship.
20.grammar: The wa- prefix is the ordinary connector 'and', linking items in a list. The -un ending is the nominative case with nunation, the case of a subject; the tanwīn shows the noun is indefinite ('churches' in general, not 'the churches').
20.root: ب-ي-ع (b-y-ʿ) — (as a place-of-worship term, a borrowed/specialised word; the root otherwise relates to exchange)

21.meaning: And synagogues — ṣalawāt is literally the plural of ṣalāt, 'prayer'; in the sense of buildings it denotes Jewish houses of prayer, synagogues.
21.grammar: The wa- prefix means 'and', continuing a list. Ṣalawāt is a sound feminine plural (the -āt pattern). The -un ending is the nominative case with nunation, marking an indefinite subject-case noun.

22.meaning: And mosques — masājid is the plural of masjid, literally 'a place of prostration (sujūd)': anywhere the forehead is placed on the ground for Allah, and by usage the mosque as a building.
22.grammar: The wa- prefix means 'and'. Masājid is a broken plural built on the 'place-noun' pattern ma- + root ('place of prostrating'). The -u ending is the nominative case, marking a subject; this plural pattern is a diptote, so it never takes tanwīn — hence -u, not -un.
22.root: س-ج-د (s-j-d) — prostrating, bowing to the ground

23.meaning: Is mentioned / is remembered — the passive of dhakara: to have one's name invoked, commemorated, kept alive on tongues and in hearts (the same root as dhikr, remembrance of Allah).
23.grammar: A present-tense passive verb: the yu- prefix with the a-vowel stem (yudhkaru, not yadhkuru) marks the passive — 'is mentioned' without naming who mentions. The final -u is the indicative mood, the ending of a plain, ongoing statement.

24.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
24.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

25.meaning: Name; the word by which a thing is called or identified. Here in the nominative, the subject form.
25.grammar: A noun. The final -u is the nominative ending (ḍamma), which typically marks the word as the subject of a sentence or the doer of an action. The initial alif is a connecting (elidable) hamza, pronounced 'is-' in isolation.
25.root: س-م-و (s-m-w) — name, height, that by which a thing is raised/known

26.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
26.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

27.meaning: An adjective/noun meaning 'many', 'much', or 'numerous' — a large quantity or great number of something.
27.grammar: Adjective/noun in the indefinite accusative, marked by the final -an (the 'tanwīn' of fatḥa). The accusative case here commonly marks an object of a verb or an indefinite quantity; the doubled-n sound (nunation) signals that the word is indefinite ('many', not 'the many').
27.root: ك-ث-ر (k-th-r) — to be much, many, abundant

28.meaning: And He will most surely help — the verb of aid-to-victory wrapped in the strongest emphasis Arabic can give a verb: an oath-style 'la-' plus the energetic '-anna' ending, together promising 'He absolutely will help'.
28.grammar: The wa- prefix means 'and'; la- is the emphatic particle used in oath-like promises. The ya- prefix means 'he'. The -anna suffix is the 'energetic' ending, attached to a future-oriented verb to give it maximum certainty — the combination la-…-anna is Arabic's most forceful way of saying 'will definitely, without fail'.

29.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
29.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

30.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
30.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.
