4.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

5.meaning: 'He causes (someone) to die' — a causative verb from the root meaning death: to bring about death, to make a living thing die. The causative form turns 'to die' into 'to put to death / to cause to die'.
5.grammar: Present/future tense. The yu- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') in the causative (form IV) pattern; the bare unending imperfect signals ongoing or future action ('he will / does cause to die'). The attached -kum is a plural object pronoun, 'you (all)'.

6.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
6.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

7.meaning: 'He gives life' or 'He brings to life' — a causative verb from the root meaning life: to make alive, to revive, to grant living existence to what was lifeless.
7.grammar: Present/future tense. The yu- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') in the causative (form IV) pattern; the imperfect without a jussive/subjunctive ending expresses ongoing or future action ('he gives / will give life'). The attached -kum is a plural object pronoun, 'you (all)'.

8.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
8.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

9.meaning: the human being, mankind — the human creature in general, marked by sociability and forgetfulness.
9.grammar: A noun for the human being, with the definite article al- ('the'). The -a ending is accusative, typically marking the direct object of a verb or following certain particles. Used generically, it denotes humankind as a type.
9.root: أ-ن-س ('-n-s) — to be sociable, familiar; humanness

10.meaning: Surely very ungrateful, certainly an ingrate — lakafūrun combines the emphatic la- with kafūr, an intensive adjective meaning extremely ungrateful or very unbelieving.

parts.en: intensive adjective, nominative indefinite: very ungrateful, extreme ingrate

10.grammar: La- is the emphatic lām reinforcing an affirmative statement. Kafūrun is the faʿūl pattern, an intensive (mubālagha) adjective meaning 'very/extremely ungrateful', in the nominative indefinite (-un tanwīn).
10.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to be ungrateful, to disbelieve, to cover (truth)

1.meaning: For every, for each, belonging to all of. Combines the preposition 'for/to' with the word for 'every/all.'
1.grammar: The preposition li- ('for/to') joined to kull ('every/each/all'). The -i ending on kull is genitive, the case required after a preposition. The combination conveys 'for every / to each.'

2.meaning: A community, nation, or people — a body of people bound together by shared faith, way of life, or origin; one collective group.
2.grammar: A feminine noun. The final -in (genitive with 'nunation') marks it as indefinite ('a community') and links it to a preceding noun or preposition ('… of a community'). The feminine -t sound surfaces before the ending.

3.meaning: We made, rendered, set up, or appointed. A completed act of making or designating, done by a group or by a majestic 'We.'
3.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb with the attached subject ending -nā, meaning 'we' did the action. 'Jaʿala' carries senses from 'to make/create' to 'to render X into Y' or 'to appoint.'
3.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, render, appoint, place

4.meaning: A rite, a prescribed way or place of worship — mansak covers the appointed act of devotion (especially sacrifice), its manner, and its place; the plural manāsik names the rites of pilgrimage.
4.grammar: A noun on the maf-ʿal pattern, which typically names the place, time, or manner of an action — so 'where/how devotion is performed', hence 'rite'. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative, the case that typically marks the object of a verb ('appointed A RITE').

5.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (referring to a group of males, or a mixed group). Because it stands on its own rather than being attached to a verb or noun, it often adds emphasis, singling out or stressing the subject ('they themselves', 'it is they who').
5.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It does not take case endings; the fixed -m simply marks the plural 'they'. Standing alone, it commonly serves to emphasise or isolate the subject.

6.meaning: '(Ones) performing it' — the active participle of nasaka: people who carry out a rite of worship; with the pronoun, 'its performers, those observing it'.

parts.en: performers of a rite (masculine plural participle; the -na of the plural drops before the pronoun)

6.grammar: nāsik is the doer-form ('one who performs a rite'). The -ū ending makes it masculine plural, 'those who perform'; the usual final -na of such plurals is dropped because the word is bound directly to the following pronoun -hu ('it') — a construction meaning 'the performers OF it'.

7.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
7.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

8.meaning: '(Let them by no means) dispute with you' — from nāzaʿa, to contend, wrangle, pull against another; the form carries a heavy emphatic ending: 'they must certainly not contend with you (about it)'.

parts.en: plural 'they' fused with the emphatic ending

8.grammar: A Form III verb (long ā after the first root letter), the pattern for actions aimed at another party — contending WITH someone. The -unna ending is the masculine-plural marker -ū(na) fused with the emphatic doubled n: together with a preceding 'let not', it yields a most emphatic prohibition, 'let them by no means...'. The attached -ka is the object 'you' (one man).

9.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
9.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

10.meaning: The matter, affair, command, or decision — either a thing being dealt with or an authoritative order that is issued. The definite article marks it as a specific, known matter.
10.grammar: A definite masculine noun. The final -i is the genitive ending, which generally links it to a preceding noun ('… of the matter') or follows a preposition.
10.root: ا-م-ر (ʾ-m-r) — to command; a matter or affair

11.meaning: And invite (people) / And call (to Allah). Refers to the act of dāʿwa — inviting people to the path of Allah and proclaiming the message.

parts.en: invite! call! summon! (masculine singular imperative, Form I)

11.grammar: Masculine imperative, Form I (daʿā — to call, to invite). The imperative of hollow verbs uses a shortened form with connecting alif.
11.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, to invite; daʿwa: a call, an invitation

12.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
12.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

13.meaning: A noun with an attached pronoun meaning 'your Lord' — the Lord/Master/Sustainer of a single person addressed. Rabb conveys an owner who creates, nurtures, sustains, and governs all that is under His care.
13.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord, Sustainer') carries the -i genitive vowel, which typically appears when the noun follows a preposition or is itself possessed by a following noun ('… of your Lord'). The suffix -ka means 'your', addressed to a single male.
13.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship; to nurture, sustain, master

14.meaning: 'Indeed you' — an emphasis particle meaning 'truly / indeed' joined to the pronoun 'you', used to open a statement with certainty and stress about the person addressed.
14.grammar: The emphasis particle 'inna' ('indeed, truly') with an attached pronoun. 'inna' adds strong assertion to a sentence and grammatically governs the following noun/pronoun in the accusative. The suffix '-ka' means 'you' (masculine singular) as its subject.

15.meaning: Surely upon — a compound formed from the emphatic particle la- and the preposition ʿalā, together stressing that the Prophet is indeed upon (a great moral character).
15.grammar: The lam is lam al-tawkīd (emphatic lam) and ʿalā is a preposition meaning 'upon'. Together la-ʿalā introduces a predicate phrase. The letter alif maqṣūra (ā) at the end of ʿalā does not take case endings.

16.meaning: Guidance — right direction, the showing of the correct way and the leading along it. The term combines pointing out the path and granting success in following it; more than mere information, it is direction toward what is right.

parts.en: indefinite (tanwin) ending on a shortened final vowel

16.grammar: An indefinite masculine singular noun. The -an (tanwin) ending marks indefiniteness — 'a guidance' rather than 'the guidance'. Because the word ends in a weak final letter, its case is not audibly distinguished, so this single form covers more than one grammatical position.

17.meaning: 'Straight / upright / undeviating' — describing something that runs true without bending or wandering; applied to a 'path' it means a direct, correct way that leads soundly to its goal.
17.grammar: An active participle (a describing word, 'straight/upright') from a verb meaning 'to be/become straight'. It is indefinite, and the -in ending is the genitive with 'tanwīn'. As a describing word it normally follows and agrees with the noun it modifies, matching that noun in being indefinite and in the genitive case.

1.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
1.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

2.meaning: 'They argued with you / disputed with you' — from jādala, to debate and contend in argument, trading words back and forth like strands twisted into a rope.
2.grammar: A past-tense Form III verb: the long ā marks action directed at another party — arguing WITH someone. The -ū ending means the subject is 'they' (a group); the attached -ka is the object 'you' (one man): 'they argued with you'.

3.meaning: 'Then say' — the command 'say!' with fa- ('then, so'), introducing the response to be given; qul is the Qur'an's frequent instruction to declare something aloud.

parts.en: helping vowel (eases pronunciation before a following consonant cluster)

3.grammar: fa- is 'then/so', tying the command to what precedes it as a response. qul is the imperative 'say!', addressed to one man — commands in Arabic have no separate 'you' word; the bare form itself is the command. The final -i is not a case ending but a helping vowel inserted so the word flows into a following word that begins with a consonant cluster.

4.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
4.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

5.meaning: 'I know' — a present-tense verb of knowing: to have certain knowledge or awareness of something.
5.grammar: A present/future (Form I) verb, first-person singular ('I'), marked by the prefix a-. This a- is the first-person agreement marker built into the conjugation, not a free-standing pronoun. The final -u marks the indicative — a plain statement of ongoing or habitual knowing.

6.meaning: A compound meaning roughly 'because of what...', 'on account of that which...', or 'by means of what...'. It joins the preposition 'with/by/because of' to a connector 'what/that which', introducing the reason or instrument for something.
6.grammar: A preposition (bi-) fused to the word mā ('what / that which'). The preposition bi- expresses cause, means, or accompaniment; combined with mā it forms a phrase pointing to the thing or fact that serves as a reason or means ('because of what...').

7.meaning: You (all) do / work / act — to carry out deeds or labor.
7.grammar: A present-tense verb (Form I). The 'ta-' prefix with the '-ūna' ending marks the second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The '-ūna' (with final 'n') is the indicative form, marking a plain ongoing or habitual statement.
7.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deeds

1.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
1.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

2.meaning: He judges / He will judge; He decides, rules, and decrees with authority — passing a binding verdict and governing a matter wisely.
2.grammar: A present/future-tense verb, 'he judges/will judge,' describing a single male subject (or 'He,' of Allah). The ya- prefix marks the third-person masculine singular ('he'), and the final -u marks the indicative mood — an actual, ongoing, or future action.
2.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge, decide, rule; wisdom and governance

3.meaning: Between you / among you; the space or relation linking the members of a group.
3.grammar: An adverb of place ('between/among') with an attached pronoun. The fixed -a ending is characteristic of such place-words; the ending -kum means 'you' for a group, so the whole means 'among you all'.
3.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation/interval; the space between two things

4.meaning: The noun 'day' — a span of time, often used for a momentous Day or appointed time; in the accusative it frequently functions as 'on the day (when…)', marking the time at which something occurs.
4.grammar: A masculine noun bearing the -a (accusative) ending. As an adverb of time this ending typically gives the sense 'on the day…', fixing the moment of an event.
4.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a period of time

5.meaning: "the Resurrection" — the standing-up of all people from death to be judged; literally the act of rising or standing up.
5.grammar: The al- prefix means "the." The -i ending (on the feminine -t) is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ("the … OF this") or follows a preposition.

6.meaning: A compound particle joining the preposition 'in/about' with the relative pronoun 'what', yielding 'in that which' or 'concerning what' — pointing to the matter or subject about which something is said or done.
6.grammar: A fixed combination of the preposition 'fī' and the indeclinable relative 'mā'. Being particles, neither takes a case ending; the phrase functions as 'in/about what…'.

7.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
7.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. As the doer is built into the suffix, the verb itself is in its base past form ('you all were').
7.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

8.meaning: 'In it / in him' — the preposition 'in, inside, within' joined to a pronoun referring to a single masculine or neuter thing. It locates something inside or as part of that referent.
8.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The pronoun -hi refers to one masculine (or grammatically masculine) thing and stands as the object of the preposition; its vowel is -i because attached pronouns take that shape after the long -i of fi. Together they answer 'in what?' or 'in whom?'.

9.meaning: 'You (all) differ / disagree' — from a verb meaning to differ, dispute, or hold conflicting views. The form addresses a group: 'you all differ from one another.'
9.grammar: A present/future-tense verb in a pattern meaning 'to differ among one another.' The ta- prefix together with the -ūna ending marks the subject as 'you all' (a group). The -na at the end signals the ordinary (indicative) present form used for a plain statement.
9.root: خ-ل-ف (kh-l-f) — to come after, differ, be at variance

1.meaning: 'Did not…?' — a particle combining a question with negation, used to ask 'Have I/has he not…?', often expecting agreement or serving as a gentle reminder.
1.grammar: An interrogative prefix 'a-' ('?') joined to the negation 'lam'. 'lam' negates a verb and places it firmly in the past ('did not'), and grammatically puts the following present-tense verb into the jussive (clipped) form. Together they form a rhetorical or confirming question.

2.meaning: You know, you come to know, you are aware — to possess knowledge or to realise/recognise something.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb in the 'you' (masculine singular) form. The ta- prefix marks a second-person singular subject ('you'). The bare ending (no final -u) is the jussive/conditional mood, the shortened form used after conditional or command-type particles rather than as a plain statement.

3.meaning: An emphatic particle meaning 'that' (as in 'I know that...') or 'indeed/surely.' It introduces a statement and gives it certainty and emphasis, presenting what follows as an established fact.
3.grammar: An emphatic particle that introduces a noun-clause ('that...'). It puts the following noun into the accusative case and lends the whole statement a sense of certainty and assertion. It typically comes after verbs of knowing, saying, or informing.

4.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
4.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

5.meaning: 'He/it knows' — a present-tense verb of knowing: to have knowledge of, be aware of, recognize, or understand something.
5.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it'). The ya- prefix marks 'he,' and the final -u marks the ordinary (indicative) present, 'he knows / does know.'
5.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — knowledge; knowing, being aware, recognizing

6.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
6.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

7.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
7.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

8.meaning: The sky or heaven — the canopy overhead; the expanse above the earth, also that which is elevated or raised over something. With the definite article it means 'the sky / the heaven'.
8.grammar: A noun with the definite article al- ('the'), in the genitive marked by the -i ending. (The 'l' of al- assimilates in sound into the following 's', a 'sun letter', though it is still written.) The genitive -i ending typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …').

9.meaning: 'And the earth' — the connective 'and' joined to 'the earth', meaning the ground, land, or the world beneath the sky.
9.grammar: The connective 'wa-' ('and') with the definite feminine noun 'al-arḍ' ('the earth'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the earth') or follows a preposition, here matching the case of what it is joined to.

10.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
10.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

11.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
11.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

12.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
12.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

13.meaning: A Book, a scripture — a written record or revealed text. In sacred usage it denotes a divinely revealed Scripture. The indefinite form means 'a book / some scripture' rather than a specific one.
13.grammar: A noun. The final -in (tanwīn) is the indefinite genitive ending: it marks the word as indefinite ('a book') and in the genitive case, the case typically used after a preposition or when one noun is linked to a preceding noun ('… of …').
13.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — to write; 'kitāb' = something written, a book

14.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
14.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

15.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
15.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

16.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
16.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
16.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

17.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
17.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

18.meaning: Easy, slight, or readily managed — something small in amount or done without difficulty.
18.grammar: An adjective of the form faʿīl. The -un ending is the indefinite nominative: it marks it as describing a subject noun, and the final -n (tanwīn) shows it is indefinite ('an easy/slight one').
18.root: ي-س-ر (y-s-r) — ease, facility, smallness of amount

1.meaning: 'And they worship / serve' — a group devoting themselves in worship and obedient service to something.
1.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') joined to a present-tense verb. The ya-…-ūna pattern marks the third-person masculine plural ('they'). The retained -na ending shows the indicative mood — a plain statement of fact ('they do worship'), as opposed to the moods that drop this -n.

2.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
2.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

3.meaning: A noun used to mean 'besides', 'other than', 'apart from', or 'short of'. It points to something or someone set apart from, or lower/lesser than, a named party. Often used in the phrase 'besides Allah'.
3.grammar: 'dūn' functions as an adverb-like noun of place/relation. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, which appears because it follows a preposition (such as 'min', 'from') and because it links to a following noun ('other than …'). It commonly heads the construction 'besides/other than [someone]'.
3.root: د-و-ن (d-w-n) — to be low/beneath, to fall short; hence 'below, other than, besides'

4.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
4.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

5.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
5.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

6.meaning: A negating particle, 'not', used specifically to deny that an action happened in the past, even though it attaches to a present-tense verb form. It turns 'you do X' into 'you did not do X'.

parts.en: did not (negation of a completed act)

6.grammar: An indeclinable particle that governs the verb after it, putting that verb into the jussive (clipped) mood and giving it past-time meaning. In short: lam + a present-form verb = 'did not [verb]'.

7.meaning: He sends down — to send something down from a higher place to a lower one, gradually or in stages. The intensive form suggests a sending-down by degrees.
7.grammar: A present-tense verb in the intensive 'fa''ala' pattern (sending down by degrees), third-person masculine singular ('he'). The vowelless final -l marks the jussive mood — the form used after certain particles (such as those for negation of the past or conditions), giving e.g. 'he did not send down' or 'let him send down'.
7.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend, come down; to send down

8.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
8.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

9.meaning: Authority, sanction, or compelling proof — power or warrant given to back something up, whether kingly authority or a decisive argument. 'Sulṭān' is authorizing power or evidence.
9.grammar: A single noun ('authority') carrying the accusative indefinite ending -an (tanwīn al-naṣb). This one ending does two things at once: the -a marks the accusative case (typically the direct object of a verb), and the final -n sound (nunation) shows the noun is indefinite ('an authority / any warrant'). The nunation is a diacritic on the case vowel, not a separable suffix, so the word stays one undivided token.

10.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
10.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

11.meaning: A special negating verb meaning 'is not / are not'. Unlike a simple particle, it behaves like a verb (frozen in the past-tense form) and serves to deny that something is the case, cancelling an assertion of being.
11.grammar: A defective verb fixed in the 3rd-person masculine singular ('he/it is not'). The final -a is its frozen ending; it does not conjugate for tense like other verbs. Grammatically it raises its subject to the nominative and puts its predicate in the accusative, functioning to negate a state of being.

12.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
12.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

13.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
13.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

14.meaning: A noun meaning 'knowledge' — sure, established knowing; awareness of facts based on evidence, the opposite of ignorance or guesswork.
14.grammar: A singular noun. The -un ending is the indefinite nominative: the 'n' sound (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('some knowledge', not 'the knowledge'), and the nominative case typically marks the subject of a sentence or the thing whose existence is being affirmed.

15.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
15.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.
15.root: — (relative pronoun / particle)

16.meaning: A prepositional phrase, 'for/to the wrongdoers' — al-ẓālimūn being those who do wrong or injustice, who put things out of their rightful place; in religious usage especially those who wrong their own souls through disbelief or transgression.
16.grammar: A definite active participle (a 'doer' noun, 'those who wrong') in the masculine plural, governed by the preposition li- ('for, to'). The plural ending -īna is the genitive/accusative plural form, required here after the preposition. The single written lām after li- is the definite article 'the', its own letter merged into the preposition.
16.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — to do wrong, oppress; injustice

17.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
17.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

18.meaning: Helper, one who aids and grants victory — an intensive form: a steady, effective supporter; in the Qur'an frequently paired with walī (protector) in statements about who can truly avail a person.
18.grammar: A noun/adjective on the intensive faʿīl pattern: not a one-time helper but one characterized by helping. The -in ending is the indefinite genitive: nunation marks 'a helper' (indefinite), and the i-vowel of the genitive typically follows a preposition or the word min ('any helper'), or links the word to a preceding noun as 'of...'. The doubled n shown at the start is simply the word's first letter assimilating to the end of the preceding word in recitation.

1.meaning: 'And when...' — a linking phrase joining 'and' to 'when', used to introduce a circumstance or a recurring situation: 'and whenever / and at the time that...'.
1.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to idhā ('when'). Idhā is a particle pointing to a time or condition, generally referring to something expected or recurring in the future ('when / whenever' it happens), and it normally introduces a following clause that states what occurs at that time.

2.meaning: It is being recited or read aloud — said of verses or scripture conveyed by voice, in an ongoing or repeated manner.

parts.en: recite/read aloud (passive stem, root letters t-l + long ā)

2.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) passive verb in the third person feminine singular ('it/she is recited'). The tu- prefix marks both the present tense and the passive voice ('is being …-ed'), so the doer is unnamed and the focus is on what undergoes the action. The stem -tlā keeps the second root consonant (t) and ends in a long ā written with ى, the shape a weak-final (defective) root takes when no further ending is attached.
2.root: ت-ل-و (t-l-w) — to recite, read aloud, follow

3.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
3.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
3.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

4.meaning: Our signs / verses — 'āyāt' are tokens, proofs, and miraculous indications that point to a deeper truth, and also the verses of revelation; with 'Our' it refers to such signs ascribed to Allah.
4.grammar: A feminine plural noun ('signs, verses') with the attached possessive 'our' = -nā. The -u vowel before the pronoun marks the subject/naming case, the form a noun takes as the doer or topic of a sentence ('Our signs [are/do...]').
4.root: أ-ي-ي (ʾ-y-y) — sign, mark, token, miraculous indication

5.meaning: Clear, manifest, self-evident — the feminine plural of 'bayyin', describing things that are plainly evident and make matters distinct; an intensive adjective implying something that clarifies and is itself unmistakable.
5.grammar: A sound feminine plural adjective. The '-in' (nunation) ending marks it indefinite and in the genitive/accusative (oblique) case, so it agrees with an indefinite feminine plural noun it describes ('clear ___').
5.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — to be clear, distinct, evident; to make plain

6.meaning: 'You know / recognize' — from ʿarafa, to know by perceiving and discerning: to recognize a thing by its marks, as one recognizes a face.
6.grammar: A present/future (imperfect) verb: the ta- prefix means the subject is 'you' (one man). The final -u is the indicative mood — the ordinary form for a plain statement of present or ongoing action, 'you recognize / will recognize'.

7.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
7.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

8.meaning: Faces — the plural of wajh (face); the front of the head, and by extension a person's countenance, where inner feeling shows outwardly.
8.grammar: A broken (internal) plural: wajh becomes wujūh by reshaping the word's vowels rather than adding a suffix. The final -i is the genitive case ending: it typically links the noun to a preceding preposition (e.g. 'in/on the faces') or joins it to another noun in an 'of'-relationship.

9.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
9.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

10.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
10.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
10.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

11.meaning: Rejection, disapproval, denial — literally 'that which is rejected/disowned.' The word munkar names anything the sound heart and revealed law refuse to accept; as a feeling on the face it means visible displeasure and hostile denial.
11.grammar: Munkar is a passive participle of the Form IV verb ankara ('to reject, disavow'), so it literally means 'that which is disavowed.' The final -a is the accusative case ending, the case a noun typically takes when it is the object of a verb ('you recognize the disapproval').
11.root: ن-ك-ر (n-k-r) — to refuse to recognize, disavow, find strange

12.meaning: Verb from the 'verb of approach' kāda, meaning 'they are about to / they almost / they nearly (do something)' — expressing that an action is on the verge of happening without (yet) being realized.

parts.en: to be on the point of, almost do (hollow stem)

12.grammar: A present-tense verb, masculine third-person plural. The full ending '-ūna' (with its 'nūn' kept) marks the plain indicative mood — a straightforward statement, 'they are on the point of …' This is one of the 'verbs of approach,' which take a following verb to mean 'almost / nearly.'
12.root: ك-و-د (k-w-d) — to be on the verge of, to almost happen

13.meaning: They pounce, assault violently — from saṭā, to spring upon someone with force, as a beast lunges at prey; a sudden violent attack driven by rage.
13.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb. The ya- prefix marks the third person in the present tense; the -ūna ending (the long ū plus -na) marks a masculine plural subject in the normal indicative mood — together they say 'they (a group of men) are attacking / are about to attack.'

14.meaning: A connector meaning 'about/concerning those who' or 'by means of those who'. It joins the preposition 'with/about' to a relative pronoun referring to a known group of male (or mixed) persons, 'those who…'.
14.grammar: The bi- is a preposition ('with', 'about', 'by means of'). 'alladhīna' is the plural relative pronoun 'those who', referring to a group of males or a mixed group; it introduces a clause describing them. Being governed by a preposition, the whole phrase functions in the genitive (the object of 'about/with').

15.meaning: They recite / they read out; they read aloud and follow word for word — especially the reciting of a revealed scripture, conveying both 'to read' and 'to follow.'
15.grammar: A present/future-tense verb meaning 'they recite,' from a defective root whose final letter is a weak wāw. The ya- prefix with the -ūna suffix marks a third-person masculine plural ('they'). Because the root ends in a weak wāw, that wāw contracts with the plural suffix to produce a single long -ū sound (so the stem's last consonant is not separately heard); the -na of -ūna is the indicative marker for an actual, ongoing, or habitual action.
15.root: ت-ل-و (t-l-w) — to recite, read aloud, follow

16.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
16.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
16.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

17.meaning: Our signs / verses. The plural of āya — a sign, token, or miraculous proof, and also a verse of revelation — with the attached 'our'.
17.grammar: A feminine plural noun ('signs / verses') with the possessive pronoun -nā ('our'). The sound feminine plural ending -āt shows -i, the case used for the genitive (linked to a following word or after a preposition) and the accusative (object of a verb); attaching -nā ('our') also places it in a possessive relationship. So it means 'signs belonging to Us'.

18.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
18.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

19.meaning: 'Shall I then inform you…?' — a challenge-question packing four pieces into one word: a question marker, the connector 'then/so,' the verb 'I tell/announce (emphatically),' and 'you all.' The verb nabba'a means to give weighty, significant news.
19.grammar: The opening a- is the interrogative hamza that turns a statement into a question; fa- ('then/so') links it to what came before. The u- on unabbi'u means 'I' (first person present), and the doubled middle letter (nabbi') marks Form II, an intensive pattern — announcing something significant. The -u before -kum is the indicative present-tense ending, and -kum is the attached object pronoun 'you all.'

20.meaning: 'Of/with evil, with something bad' — the preposition 'with/of' joined to the noun-adjective 'evil, badness.' It refers to something bad or harmful in itself (this is the plain noun for evil, not a comparative; the comparative 'worse' would be a different form, أَشَرّ).
20.grammar: A preposition bi- ('with, of') attached to a noun/adjective meaning 'evil, badness.' The -in ending (written as nunation, an 'n' sound) marks the noun as indefinite ('an evil, some badness') and in the genitive case — the case a noun takes after a preposition like bi-. It is a plain noun, not a comparative form.
20.root: ش-ر-ر (sh-r-r) — evil, badness, wickedness

21.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
21.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

22.meaning: A demonstrative meaning 'that' — a pointing word that singles out something distant or already mentioned, addressed to a group of people ('that, O you [plural]').
22.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that', built from the base 'dhā' plus the distance-marker 'l-' and the plural-addressee particle '-kum' ('you all'). The final 'u' on '-kumu' is a connecting vowel used when the next word begins with a definite article. It does not change for case.

23.meaning: The Fire — a definite noun for fire; frequently the term for the blazing punishment of the Hereafter (Hell).
23.grammar: Definite noun: 'al-' is 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the following 'n', heard as 'an-nār'). The '-u' ending is nominative, the case typically marking the subject of a sentence or the doer of an action.

24.meaning: 'He promised it' — the verb waʿada, to give a promise or binding assurance, with a feminine object pronoun ('it/her') attached.
24.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb: the -a ending on waʿada marks 'he' (third person masculine singular) in the past. The initial wa- is part of the root itself, not the word 'and.' The suffix -hā is the attached feminine object pronoun, 'it/her' — referring to some feminine noun previously mentioned.

25.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
25.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

26.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
26.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

27.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
27.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
27.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

28.meaning: And how evil / wretched (it is)! — wa joined to biʾsa, a fixed verb of blame used to condemn something as bad, the opposite of niʿma ('how excellent'). It expresses strong disapproval.
28.grammar: Conjunction wa- ('and') plus biʾsa, a frozen verb of blame ('how wretched is …') that does not change for tense. It introduces strong condemnation of whatever follows as its subject, the counterpart of niʿma ('how good is …').

29.meaning: Al-maṣīr — the destination, the place or state one finally comes to; the journey's end or ultimate outcome to which things return.
29.grammar: A definite noun of place/result on the pattern mafʿil, with the long ī arising from the weak root letter yāʾ (ص-ي-ر). The final -u ending is nominative, the case used for the subject of a sentence or what something ultimately is. The word denotes the final place or state to which one comes.
29.root: ص-ي-ر (ṣ-y-r) — to become, come to, end up at

1.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: 'The people / mankind' — human beings collectively, people in general, humanity.
2.grammar: A collective noun with the definite article al- ('the'); the article's 'l' assimilates into the following 'n' (al-nās → an-nās). The -u ending marks the nominative case — the case used for the subject of a sentence or the basic naming form of a noun.
2.root: ن-و-س / أ-ن-س (n-w-s / ʾ-n-s) — humankind, people, sociability

3.meaning: Is presented, is set forth — ḍuriba is the passive perfect of ḍaraba (to strike, to coin, to present). In the context of ḍaraba mathal it means 'an example/parable is presented/set forth'.

parts.en: perfect passive verb, 3rd person masculine singular: was presented, was set forth, was coined (as an example)

3.grammar: Ḍuriba is the Form I passive perfect (the passive is formed by changing the vowels: ḍaraba → ḍuriba), third-person masculine singular. The passive voice means 'it was presented/struck'. Ḍaraba mathal is the standard phrase for 'to coin a parable/set forth an example'.
3.root: ض-ر-ب (ḍ-r-b) — to strike; to coin (an expression/parable); to set forth an example

4.meaning: A likeness, parable, example — mathal is a comparison struck to make a truth vivid: an illustrative similitude held up so the listener can grasp an abstract reality through a concrete picture.
4.grammar: The -un ending does two jobs: the -u part is the nominative case (the case of a sentence's subject or of a noun being announced/presented), and the -n (tanwīn, the doubled vowel sign) marks indefiniteness — 'a parable,' not 'the parable.'

5.meaning: A command addressed to a group: 'so/then listen!' The base verb istamaʿa means to listen attentively, to lend one's ear and take in what is said — stronger and more deliberate than merely hearing. The opening fa- adds the sense of 'and so' or 'then', linking the command to something preceding it as a consequence.
5.grammar: A command (imperative) directed at more than one person. The -ū ending marks a masculine plural addressee, i.e. 'you all (do this)'. The prefixed fa- is a connecting particle meaning 'then / so / and as a result', tying the order to what came before. The verb belongs to Form X (istafʿala, pattern istaf'ala, with the characteristic ist- prefix), which often adds the sense of seeking or applying oneself — hence active, attentive listening.

6.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
6.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

7.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
7.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

8.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
8.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

9.meaning: A verb meaning 'you (all) call upon, invoke, summon, or pray to.' The root spans calling out, naming, inviting, and supplicating — especially calling on someone for help.
9.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ta- prefix with the -ūna ending marks 'you all' (masculine plural) as the doers. The final -na is the indicative marker, signalling an ongoing or habitual action (a complete, non-shortened present-tense verb).
9.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, invoke, summon, pray

10.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
10.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

11.meaning: A noun used to mean 'besides', 'other than', 'apart from', or 'short of'. It points to something or someone set apart from, or lower/lesser than, a named party. Often used in the phrase 'besides Allah'.
11.grammar: 'dūn' functions as an adverb-like noun of place/relation. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, which appears because it follows a preposition (such as 'min', 'from') and because it links to a following noun ('other than …'). It commonly heads the construction 'besides/other than [someone]'.
11.root: د-و-ن (d-w-n) — to be low/beneath, to fall short; hence 'below, other than, besides'

12.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
12.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

13.meaning: 'Never / will not' — a particle that negates a future action emphatically. Lan denies that something will ever happen, stronger and more absolute than a simple 'not'.
13.grammar: A negating particle that applies to present-tense verbs to deny them in the future ('will never…'). Grammatically it also puts the following verb into the subjunctive mood, which clips that verb's ending to a short -a. Lan itself does not change.

14.meaning: '(They) create' — the verb khalaqa, to create, to bring into being; the distinctive divine act of originating something.
14.grammar: A present-tense plural verb ('they create'), but note the ending: the plural is just -ū with no final -na. That dropped -na is a mood marker — it shows the verb stands in a non-indicative mood (subjunctive or jussive), the shortened shape this verb type takes when governed by a preceding particle such as lan ('never will') or lam ('did not'). The form itself only signals that some such governing word is at work; any sense of 'never' or 'not' comes from that separate particle, not from the verb.
14.root: خ-ل-ق (kh-l-q) — to create, bring into being

15.meaning: A fly — dhubāb, the common housefly; in Arabic idiom the very emblem of what is tiny, weak, and contemptible.
15.grammar: The -an ending combines the accusative case -a (the case a noun takes as the object of a verb — the thing created, in typical use) with tanwīn (-n), which marks indefiniteness: 'a fly,' any single fly.
15.root: ذ-ب-ب (dh-b-b) — fly; to buzz, drive off

16.meaning: 'And even if; even though' — combines 'and' with the conditional 'if' to introduce a supposition, often a far-fetched or extreme one, conceding 'even supposing that…'. The final vowel is a connecting vowel added for ease of pronunciation.

parts.en: if (even if); '-i' is a helping vowel

16.grammar: Two particles joined: 'wa-' ('and') plus 'law' ('if'), the latter introducing a hypothetical condition. 'Law' has no case ending; the '-i' at the end is not grammatical but a connecting vowel inserted to avoid two unvowelled consonants meeting when the next word begins with the article.

17.meaning: 'They gathered together' — Form VIII of jamaʿa (to gather): to assemble, band together, combine forces as one body for a common purpose.
17.grammar: A past-tense verb in Form VIII, whose infixed -ta- (the t inside ijTAmaʿa) gives the sense of doing something jointly or for oneself — here 'come together as a group.' The initial i- is only a helping vowel to make the cluster pronounceable. The -ū ending marks a masculine plural subject in the past: 'they gathered.'

18.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
18.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

19.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
19.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

20.meaning: '(If) it snatches from them' — the verb salaba, to snatch away, strip, rob someone of something by force, with 'them' attached as the persons robbed.
20.grammar: A present-tense verb with the ya- prefix marking 'he/it' (third person masculine singular). The stem ends with no vowel (yaslub, not yaslubu) — that vowel-less ending is the jussive mood, the clipped form a verb takes inside a conditional ('if it snatches…'). The suffix -humu is the attached object pronoun 'them' (its final -u is just a linking vowel before a following word).
20.root: س-ل-ب (s-l-b) — to snatch, strip away, plunder

21.meaning: The fly — dhubāb with the definite article: the specific fly just spoken of, the proverbially feeble creature.
21.grammar: The article al- assimilates to the 'sun letter' dh, so it is heard as adh-dh (written l- in transliteration but pronounced doubled). The final -u is the nominative case ending — the case of the doer of a verb or the subject of a sentence: the fly as the one performing an action.
21.root: ذ-ب-ب (dh-b-b) — fly; to buzz, drive off

22.meaning: A thing; something or anything. With a negation it commonly amounts to 'nothing at all.'
22.grammar: A singular masculine noun, indefinite ('a thing'). The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative, often used here as an object or an adverbial 'in any respect / at all.'

23.meaning: 'Not' — a particle of negation. Depending on context it denies a present fact, forbids an action, or rules something out ('do not / there is no').
23.grammar: A negating particle, 'not / no'. It is used to deny or prohibit — negating present-tense statements, expressing 'there is no...', or, with a command form, forbidding an action ('do not...').

24.meaning: '(They could not) rescue it' — Form X of the root n-q-dh: to seek to rescue, to try to recover or retrieve something seized, with 'it' attached as the thing to be recovered.
24.grammar: A Form X verb: the sta- element characteristically means 'to seek or try to do' the root's action — here, to try to get something rescued back. The plural marker is bare -ū with no -na: that shortened ending is the clipped (jussive/subjunctive) mood used in negated or conditional clauses ('they could not…'). The final -hu is the object pronoun 'it.'

25.meaning: 'From it / out of it / from him'. It combines the preposition 'from / out of' with the pronoun 'it/him'.
25.grammar: The preposition min ('from / out of', indicating origin or source) with the attached pronoun -hu ('it' / 'him'), referring to a singular masculine thing or person. As object of the preposition, the pronoun is in the oblique form.
25.root: — (no triliteral root; a preposition with a pronoun)

26.meaning: 'Is feeble, has grown weak' — the stative verb ḍaʿufa, to be or become weak, lacking all strength; the pattern with inner u (ḍaʿufa) describes an inherent quality rather than a one-off act.
26.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb: the final -a marks a third person masculine singular subject, 'he/it was (or has proved to be) weak.' Verbs of this faʿula vowel-pattern typically express a lasting state or quality rather than a single event.

27.meaning: The seeker — the active participle of ṭalaba (to seek, pursue, demand): the one doing the seeking or pursuing.
27.grammar: Ṭālib is the active-participle pattern fāʿil, which turns a verb into 'the one who does it' — seeker. The article al- assimilates to the sun letter ṭ (pronounced aṭ-ṭ). The final -u is the nominative case ending, the case of a sentence's subject: 'the seeker (is)…'.

28.meaning: 'And the one sought' — the passive participle of ṭalaba: the object of pursuit, the one being sought; the mirror-image of 'the seeker.'
28.grammar: Maṭlūb is the passive-participle pattern mafʿūl, which turns a verb into 'the one to whom it is done' — the sought one. Wa- is the simple connector 'and,' joining this noun to a preceding one. The final -u is the nominative case, matching the noun it is paired with as co-subject.

1.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
1.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

2.meaning: 'they esteemed / assessed / gave due measure to'. Past-tense verb from qadara, whose core idea is to measure, estimate, or assign proper worth and proportion. The 'they' is a masculine group.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb. The suffix -ū marks a third-person masculine plural subject: 'they (did)'. The final written alif after the -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.
2.root: ق-د-ر (q-d-r) — to measure, determine, appraise; capacity and due proportion

3.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
3.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

4.meaning: Due right, just measure, rightful claim; that which is true and rightly owed — here used to mean 'as is truly its due'.
4.grammar: A noun meaning 'truth, right, due'. The final -a (accusative) often marks the object of a verb, and in a possessive phrase like this it commonly conveys the sense 'with the full right/due OF …', i.e. as something deserves to be done.
4.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right, that which is due and real

5.meaning: 'his/its proper measure / worth / due estimation'. The noun qadr means the true measure, value, or rank of something — its proper standing — joined to the pronoun 'his/its'.
5.grammar: This is a possession phrase (iḍāfa): qadr is the possessed term (mudāf) and the attached pronoun -hi is the possessor (mudāf ilayh). In an iḍāfa, the possessed term takes whatever case its own role in the sentence requires, while the possessor term always stands in the genitive. The -i vowel on the pronoun (-hi, lengthened in recitation to -hī) reflects that genitive. The pronoun means 'his' or 'its', linking the measure to its owner.
5.root: ق-د-ر (q-d-r) — to measure, determine; due proportion and worth

6.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
6.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

7.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
7.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

8.meaning: 'Indeed strong / truly powerful' — possessing real strength, might, and capability.
8.grammar: The adjective qawiyy ('strong, powerful') with the emphatic prefix la- ('surely, indeed') that affirms and stresses the description. The final -un ending is the nominative case with indefiniteness, the form used for a predicate ('he is indeed strong'); the nunation (-n) marks it as indefinite.

9.meaning: Mighty, invincible, and supremely honoured; one who possesses overwhelming power and dignity such that none can overcome or resist Him. As a divine descriptor it conveys unassailable might joined with exalted worth.
9.grammar: A descriptive noun (adjective) on an intensive pattern, conveying a deep, enduring quality. The -un ending is indefinite and nominative: it typically marks the word as a subject or as a predicate describing something ("is mighty").

1.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
1.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

2.meaning: 'He chooses, selects' — Form VIII of ṣafā (to be pure, clear): to pick out the choicest and purest for oneself; the verb behind muṣṭafā, 'the Chosen One.'

parts.en: choose the best for oneself, select (Form VIII)

2.grammar: A present-tense verb, third person masculine singular ('he chooses'), marked by the ya- prefix. The ṭ in the middle is actually the Form VIII -ta- infix, which changes to ṭ after the emphatic ṣ; that infix adds the sense of doing something for oneself — selecting the pure and best. The verb's root ends in a weak letter, so the word closes with the long vowel -ī rather than a case-style vowel; this long -ī is its normal present-tense (indicative) shape.
2.root: ص-ف-و (ṣ-f-w) — to be pure, clear, choice

3.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
3.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

4.meaning: 'The angels' — the plural of 'angel': the noble created beings who serve and obey Allah and carry out His commands.
4.grammar: A definite noun: al- means 'the.' Malāʾika is the broken (irregular) plural of malak, 'angel.' The final tā' marbūṭa (ة) is part of this collective/group plural's standard form — it is not a 'plural' marker by itself. The case vowel on it is the genitive -i (heard as -ti), the ending used after a preposition or to link 'of,' signalling the noun is the object of a preceding preposition.
4.root: م-ل-ك (m-l-k) — the root underlying malak, 'angel' (a messenger/emissary)

5.meaning: 'messengers' — envoys, those sent by Allah bearing a message to people.
5.grammar: The broken (irregular) plural of rasūl ('messenger'). The -an ending is accusative with tanwīn, typically marking the word as a direct object and indefinite ('messengers').

6.meaning: A connector meaning 'and', joined to the preposition 'from / of', introducing a portion or origin — 'and from' or 'and among'.
6.grammar: Two particles: wa- ('and') plus the preposition min ('from, of, among'). Min normally appears as 'min', but its final vowel shifts to 'mina' when the next word begins with the definite article, simply to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

7.meaning: Humankind, people, mankind — the collective of human beings.
7.grammar: A collective noun ('people, mankind') carrying the definite article al- ('the'); the 'l' of the article assimilates into the following 'n', doubling it (al-nās → an-nās). The genitive ending -i marks the word as governed by a preposition or as the second term of a possessive.
7.root: ء-ن-س (ʾ-n-s) — humankind, sociability, familiarity; the word for 'people' is most commonly traced to this root (related to insān, 'human being')

8.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
8.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

9.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
9.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

10.meaning: An intensive descriptive noun meaning 'All-Hearing' or 'ever-hearing' — one who hears fully, constantly, and perfectly; as a divine attribute, the One who hears every sound and supplication.
10.grammar: An intensive adjective/noun on the faʿīl pattern, conveying constant, abundant hearing. The final -u vowel is nominative, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate that describes the subject ('… is all-hearing').

11.meaning: 'All-Seeing / fully observant' — one who sees clearly and with complete insight; as a divine attribute, the One who perceives all things.
11.grammar: An intensive adjective on the faʿīl pattern, denoting one who possesses sight to a high degree — 'all-seeing'. The -un ending (tanwīn) is nominative plus indefiniteness, the form used for a subject or for a predicate ('[He] is all-seeing').

1.meaning: 'He/it knows' — a present-tense verb of knowing: to have knowledge of, be aware of, recognize, or understand something.
1.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it'). The ya- prefix marks 'he,' and the final -u marks the ordinary (indicative) present, 'he knows / does know.'
1.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — knowledge; knowing, being aware, recognizing

2.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
2.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

3.meaning: Between; in the midst of two things. An adverb of place marking the space separating or lying among parties or points.
3.grammar: An adverb of place ('between'). It always ends in -a and grammatically governs what follows it, putting the following noun(s) into the genitive 'of' relationship. It does not change to show 'the' or a case of its own; the fixed -a is simply how this word is formed.
3.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies between

4.meaning: Their hands. The plural noun 'hands' carrying the masculine plural possessive 'their'; often used idiomatically for what people do, produce, or are responsible for through their own deeds.
4.grammar: A plural noun with an attached possessive pronoun '-him' meaning 'their' (a group of males, or mixed). 'aydī' is the irregular ('broken') plural of 'yad' (hand). The pronoun ending makes the whole construction definite and possessed; the 'i'-coloured stem before the suffix reflects its genitive/possessed state, the form typically following a preposition or standing as object.

5.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
5.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

6.meaning: 'behind them' — the space or position to the rear of a group; also figuratively what lies after them, what awaits them, or what is hidden from them.
6.grammar: An adverb of place ('behind') with the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The -a ending is accusative, the case regularly used for adverbs of place and time, indicating the location 'behind.'
6.root: خ-ل-ف (kh-l-f) — to be behind, come after, succeed

7.meaning: And to / and toward; a connector "and" joined with a preposition expressing direction or destination toward which something moves or is referred.
7.grammar: A preposition meaning "to/toward," prefixed with the connector wa- ("and"). Being a preposition, it puts the noun that follows it into the genitive case (the "…toward X" relationship). It has no case ending of its own.

8.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
8.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

9.meaning: It is returned / brought back; a present-tense passive action of being sent or referred back to a source or destination.
9.grammar: A present/ongoing verb in the passive voice, so the action is done to the subject ("is returned/brought back"). The tu- prefix marks a third-person feminine singular (or non-human plural) subject ("it/they"). The final -u ending signals the indicative mood, used for stating an action.

10.meaning: The matters, affairs, or things; the plural of "affair/matter," denoting all the various businesses, situations, or commands taken together.
10.grammar: A definite plural noun with prefixed al- ("the"), the plural of the word for "matter/affair." The -u ending is nominative: it typically marks the word as a subject or as the doer/topic of an action.

1.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
